santorini.name: Santorini
santorini.description: Santorini delivers a visual drama unlike anywhere else in the Mediterranean. White-washed clifftop villages cascade down volcanic cliffs, blue-domed churches catch the Aegean light, and the sunsets at Oia draw crowds from around the world. Beneath the Instagram glamour lies a sophisticated island — world-class Assyrtiko wines from volcanic soil, a remarkable Bronze Age city at Akrotiri, and some of the most romantic restaurants in Europe.
santorini.funfact: Santorini's eruption around 1600 BC was one of the largest in human history — some historians believe it inspired the legend of Atlantis.

sights.name: Oia Village
sights.desc: The iconic clifftop village with world-famous sunsets, blue-domed churches, and cave hotels carved into the caldera rim. Arrive two hours early for sunset.

sights.name: Akrotiri Archaeological Site
sights.desc: A Minoan Bronze Age city preserved under volcanic ash — the 'Pompeii of the Aegean'. Intact frescoes and multi-storey buildings from 3,600 years ago.

sights.name: Ancient Thera
sights.desc: Ruins of a Hellenistic city on a mountain ridge with sweeping 360° island views. Less visited than Akrotiri but equally impressive.

sights.name: Fira Capital
sights.desc: The main town on the caldera edge. Great for cafés, boutiques, and the cable car down to the old port.

sights.name: Pyrgos Medieval Village
sights.desc: Hilltop village with Venetian castle ruins, labyrinthine alleys, and panoramic views. Excellent local wineries nearby.

beaches.name: Red Beach
beaches.desc: Dramatic red volcanic cliffs meeting black sand and azure water near Akrotiri. One of the most unique beaches in Europe.

beaches.name: Perissa
beaches.desc: Long organised black-sand beach with sunbeds, tavernas, and watersports. Great value and easy access.

beaches.name: Perivolos
beaches.desc: Extension of Perissa — slightly less crowded with beach bars and clubs.

beaches.name: Vlychada
beaches.desc: Otherworldly white volcanic ash cliffs frame this quiet beach. One of the most unusual spots on the island.

beaches.name: Ammoudi Bay
beaches.desc: Tiny fishing port below Oia. Swim off the rocks and watch the fishing boats. Exceptional tavernas above.

restaurants.name: Selene
restaurants.note: Michelin-listed. Celebrates Santorinian produce in elegant tasting menus.

restaurants.name: Metaxi Mas
restaurants.note: Legendary no-frills spot loved by locals and food critics. Book two weeks ahead.

restaurants.name: Kapari Wine Restaurant
restaurants.note: Perched over the caldera with an exceptional Assyrtiko wine list.

restaurants.name: Oia Castle Restaurant
restaurants.note: Unbeatable caldera view terrace. Arrive for sunset.

restaurants.name: Dimitris Ammoudi Fish Tavern
restaurants.note: Fresh catch served at the tiny port below Oia. Book the table right on the water.

restaurants.name: Lucky's Souvlakis
restaurants.note: Best budget meal on the island. Locals queue for the souvlaki wraps.

restaurants.name: Koukoumavlos
restaurants.note: Avant-garde dishes using Santorinian ingredients. One of the most innovative menus.

restaurants.name: To Psaraki
restaurants.note: Hidden gem at the marina. Superb grilled octopus and fresh fish.

restaurants.name: Nicola's Meze Wine Bar
restaurants.note: Great Assyrtiko wine and classic mezze in the narrow alleys of Oia.

restaurants.name: Volcano Blue
restaurants.note: Dramatic caldera-edge terrace. Solid cooking — the view is worth booking for.

rentals.name: Multiple agencies in Fira & Oia
rentals.desc: Essential for reaching Akrotiri, Perissa, and Vlychada. Compact car recommended for narrow roads.

rentals.name: Moto Santorini & others
rentals.desc: ATVs hugely popular for the narrow volcanic roads. Min. age 18 with licence.

rentals.name: Caldera Yachting
rentals.desc: Catamaran tours of the caldera, volcano island, and hot springs. Full-day and sunset options.

rentals.name: Sunset Oia Transfers
rentals.desc: Shared and private transfers between Fira, Oia, and the airport/port.

accommodation.why: Most romantic — clifftop cave hotels with plunge pools and caldera views. Quieter at night than Fira.
Highest village on the caldera — arguably the best views. Fewer tourists than Oia.
Main town — best transport hub, widest choice of restaurants and nightlife.
South coast by the black sand beaches. More relaxed, better value.

tips.title: July & August are extremely hot and crowded
tips.text: Peak season brings 35°C+ heat and massive crowds. May–June or September–October are far better.

tips.title: Oia sunset crowds are intense
tips.text: The famous sunset draws thousands. Arrive 2 hours early or watch from Imerovigli instead.

tips.title: Public buses are cheap but infrequent
tips.text: KTEL buses (€1.80/ride) run limited schedules. A rental car gives much more freedom.

tips.title: Santorini wine is exceptional
tips.text: Volcanic soil produces some of the best Assyrtiko white wine in Greece. Visit Santo Wines or Domaine Sigalas.

tips.title: Donkeys in Fira — be aware
tips.text: The cable car (€6) or walking is recommended over the controversial donkey rides.

milos.name: Milos
milos.description: Milos is the Cyclades' best-kept secret. With over 70 beaches shaped by volcanic activity into surreal colours, every cove feels like a genuine discovery. The white pumice formations at Sarakiniko look like a moonscape, the sea caves at Kleftiko are only accessible by boat, and the colourful syrmata boat garages at Klima are among Greece's most photographed villages. Less developed than Santorini, it offers better prices and a rare feeling of having found somewhere special.
milos.funfact: The Venus de Milo statue — now in the Louvre — was discovered by a farmer on Milos in 1820.

sights.name: Sarakiniko Beach
sights.desc: The lunar landscape of white volcanic rock meeting brilliant blue water. One of the most photographed spots in Greece. Visit at sunrise.

sights.name: Kleftiko Sea Caves
sights.desc: Accessible only by boat — towering white rock formations and emerald sea caves. Extraordinary snorkelling.

sights.name: Klima Fishing Village
sights.desc: Colourful boat garages (syrmata) built into the sea-level cliffs. A uniquely Milos phenomenon — photograph at sunrise.

sights.name: Catacombs of Milos
sights.desc: One of the most important early Christian monuments in Greece, carved into the rock.

sights.name: Plaka Village
sights.desc: The hilltop capital with a Venetian castle, panoramic island views, and charming alleys.

beaches.name: Sarakiniko
beaches.desc: Lunar white rock formations — more spectacle than swimming beach. Iconic and unmissable.

beaches.name: Tsigrado
beaches.desc: Tiny hidden cove via a ladder through a cliff crack. Spectacular turquoise water — arrive early.

beaches.name: Firiplaka
beaches.desc: Wide sandy beach with colourful cliffs. Sunbeds, calm clear water — good for families.

beaches.name: Papafragas
beaches.desc: Three sea caves forming natural swimming pools — you swim into the caves from the rocks above.

beaches.name: Paliochori
beaches.desc: Long beach with geothermal activity warming the sand and water. A unique warm-sand experience.

restaurants.name: Aragosta
restaurants.note: Best seafood in Adamas port. Grilled fresh catch, great octopus, local wine.

restaurants.name: O!Hamos
restaurants.note: Tiny, authentic, beloved by locals. Off the tourist track — reservation essential.

restaurants.name: Utopia Cafe
restaurants.note: The most charming café on the island. Great coffee and local pastries.

restaurants.name: Barko
restaurants.note: Right at the colourful syrmata of Klima. One of the most atmospheric tables in Greece.

restaurants.name: Medusa Restaurant
restaurants.note: Hillside terrace with sunset views. Excellent mezze and grilled meats.

restaurants.name: Sirocco
restaurants.note: By the fishing harbour in Pollonia. Great while watching ferries to Kimolos.

restaurants.name: Nefeli
restaurants.note: Local favourite for home-cooked Greek food at honest prices.

restaurants.name: Floisvos
restaurants.note: Reliable harbour taverna. Fresh fish priced by weight, good local wine.

restaurants.name: To Hani
restaurants.note: In the old capital village, hidden from tourists. Rustic, genuine, delicious.

restaurants.name: Mikro Cafe
restaurants.note: Tiny alley café in Plaka. Excellent Greek coffee and homemade sweets.

rentals.name: Milos Rent a Car
rentals.desc: Essential — many beaches only reachable by car or 4x4. Book early.

rentals.name: Milos Boats
rentals.desc: Self-drive boats to reach Kleftiko and hidden coves. The best way to explore.

rentals.name: Milos Explorer Cruises
rentals.desc: Guided day trips to Kleftiko, Tsigrado, and the sea caves with snorkelling. Lunch included.

rentals.name: Moto Milos
rentals.desc: Good for the main coastal routes. Some beach tracks need an ATV.

accommodation.why: The hilltop capital — beautiful architecture, fantastic views, good cafés.
Most practical base. Best for ferry access and widest range of hotels.
Charming fishing village on the north coast. Great seafood and boat trip access.
Quiet south coast base near Firiplaka and Paliochori. Best for beach-focused visitors.

tips.title: Book boat tours immediately
tips.text: Kleftiko boat tours fill up weeks ahead in July–August. Book as soon as you confirm your dates.

tips.title: A car or ATV is essential
tips.text: Milos has almost no public transport to its beaches. Rent from day one.

tips.title: Milos is fantastic for snorkelling
tips.text: The volcanic waters and sea caves make it one of the best snorkelling destinations in Greece.

tips.title: Some beaches require 4x4 or hiking
tips.text: Tsigrado and Gerontas need a rough track or short hike. Check conditions first.

tips.title: Ferry connections can be slow
tips.text: Served from Piraeus (7 hrs) and a small airport with summer connections. Book ahead.

crete.name: Crete
crete.description: Crete is Greece at its most complete. The fifth-largest island in the Mediterranean has the climate of North Africa, dramatic gorge landscapes, and Caribbean-quality beaches — all in one place. It is Greece's culinary heartland with a distinct food culture and some of the best olive oil in the world. Ancient Minoan palaces, Venetian harbour towns, mountain villages unchanged for centuries, and more caves, gorges, and pink-sand lagoons than you can visit in a single trip.
crete.funfact: The Minoan civilisation on Crete (2700–1450 BC) was Europe's first advanced civilisation — they had indoor plumbing before Rome was founded.

sights.name: Palace of Knossos
sights.desc: Europe's oldest city and the legendary labyrinth of the Minotaur. A window into Minoan civilisation. Visit early morning.

sights.name: Chania Old Town & Venetian Harbour
sights.desc: The most beautiful city in Crete. The crescent Venetian harbour with its lighthouse and minarets is among the finest waterfronts in the Mediterranean.

sights.name: Samaria Gorge
sights.desc: Europe's longest gorge — a 16km hike through dramatic limestone cliffs to the Libyan Sea. Requires a full day.

sights.name: Spinalonga Island
sights.desc: A former Venetian fortress and Europe's last active leper colony (closed 1957). Reached by boat from Elounda.

sights.name: Rethymno Old Town
sights.desc: A beautifully preserved Venetian and Ottoman town with a lighthouse, massive fortress, and atmospheric evening dining.

beaches.name: Elafonisi
beaches.desc: Shallow pink-tinged sand lagoon in the far southwest. One of the most beautiful beaches in Europe. Arrive before 10am.

beaches.name: Balos Lagoon
beaches.desc: Turquoise lagoon with a sandy island — by boat from Kissamos or rough 4x4 road. Flamingos visit in spring.

beaches.name: Preveli Beach
beaches.desc: River meets the sea beneath gorge cliffs — palm trees and crystal water. A short hike adds to the adventure.

beaches.name: Falassarna
beaches.desc: Wide, wild beach on the northwest coast with consistently turquoise water. Less crowded than Elafonisi.

beaches.name: Vai Palm Beach
beaches.desc: Europe's only natural palm forest behind a golden beach. Unique and beautiful — go early.

restaurants.name: Tamam
restaurants.note: In a converted Turkish bath. One of the most beloved restaurants in Chania.

restaurants.name: Thalassino Ageri
restaurants.note: Romantic waterfront setting. Considered one of the finest fish restaurants in Greece.

restaurants.name: Peskesi
restaurants.note: Farm-to-table in a beautiful mansion. Ingredients from their own farm.

restaurants.name: Avli
restaurants.note: Romantic garden in Rethymno old town. The best restaurant on the middle coast.

restaurants.name: Kouris
restaurants.note: Mountain village taverna serving legendary lamb on the spit. Worth a special trip.

restaurants.name: To Maridaki
restaurants.note: Brilliant, affordable seafood. Tiny, noisy, packed with locals.

restaurants.name: To Karnagio
restaurants.note: Tiny old-town ouzo bar. Outstanding seafood mezze at honest prices.

restaurants.name: Ella
restaurants.note: Contemporary Cretan cooking. Great wine list featuring Vidiano and Kotsifali.

restaurants.name: Kipos
restaurants.note: Garden restaurant by the sea. Good base for Spinalonga visits.

restaurants.name: Minos Beach
restaurants.note: Romantic waterside dining. Good base for exploring east Crete.

rentals.name: Creta Cars (multiple locations)
rentals.desc: Absolutely essential for exploring Crete. Rent for your full stay.

rentals.name: Jeep Crete
rentals.desc: For Balos, the Libyan coast road, and mountain villages. Opens up a different Crete.

rentals.name: Balos & Elafonisi Boat Tours
rentals.desc: Daily boats to Balos from Kissamos. Essential if you lack a 4x4 for the rough Balos road.

rentals.name: Cretan Moto (multiple)
rentals.desc: Good for individual towns and nearby areas. Not recommended for the full island.

accommodation.why: The most beautiful city in Crete. Best old town, harbour, restaurants. Perfect base for western Crete.
Best-preserved Venetian old town. Central location — good for both east and west.
Capital and main transport hub. Essential for Knossos. Less charming but very convenient.
Luxury resort area — upscale hotels, spa resorts, Spinalonga day trips.

tips.title: Crete is very large — plan by region
tips.text: Driving from Chania to Sitia takes over 3 hours. Plan your trip by region.

tips.title: Samaria Gorge requires serious preparation
tips.text: The 16km hike takes 5–7 hours. Proper shoes, plenty of water, early start — non-negotiable.

tips.title: Cretan cuisine is world-class
tips.text: Eat at places with handwritten menus and local wine. The Cretan diet is one of the healthiest in the world.

tips.title: Cretan wine is underrated
tips.text: Unique varieties (Vidiano, Kotsifali, Dafni) producing excellent wines largely unknown outside Greece.

tips.title: Mountain roads can be very challenging
tips.text: South coast villages and gorge access roads are steep and narrow. Stick to the main highway if unsure.

rhodes.name: Rhodes
rhodes.description: Rhodes is the undisputed queen of the Dodecanese — an island where a UNESCO-listed medieval city built by the Knights of St John sits minutes from turquoise beaches, and where the interior villages look like something from a postcard of rural Greece from 50 years ago. The old town of Rhodes is among the best-preserved medieval walled cities in the world, and the village of Lindos, with its ancient acropolis glowing white above a perfect bay, is one of the most beautiful sights in the whole of the Mediterranean.
rhodes.ferry: Athens (Piraeus) — 14 hrs ferry / Piraeus, Thessaloniki, Crete connections
rhodes.funfact: The Colossus of Rhodes — a giant statue of the sun god Helios — was one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World, standing at the entrance to Rhodes harbour.

sights.name: Medieval City of Rhodes
sights.desc: A UNESCO World Heritage walled city built by the Knights of St John — the most complete medieval city in Europe. The Street of the Knights is extraordinary.

sights.name: Lindos Village & Acropolis
sights.desc: A dazzling white village below an ancient acropolis with a Temple of Athena Lindia and sweeping views. One of the most beautiful villages in Greece.

sights.name: Valley of the Butterflies
sights.desc: A magical wooded valley where thousands of Jersey Tiger moths gather in summer. A serene and beautiful natural detour.

sights.name: Anthony Quinn Bay
sights.desc: A small, idyllic cove named after the actor who bought the surrounding land after filming The Guns of Navarone here. Crystal-clear water.

sights.name: Ancient Kamiros
sights.desc: The ruins of one of the three ancient cities of Rhodes — less visited than Lindos but beautifully set on a hillside above the sea.

beaches.name: Lindos Beach
beaches.desc: Below the famous white village — a beautiful sandy bay in a perfect natural amphitheatre. Busy but beautiful.

beaches.name: Tsambika Beach
beaches.desc: Wide arc of fine golden sand on the east coast. Clear warm water, easy access, good facilities. One of the best family beaches on the island.

beaches.name: Anthony Quinn Bay
beaches.desc: Tiny, sheltered cove of crystal-clear water with dramatic rock formations. Small but extraordinarily beautiful.

beaches.name: Prasonisi
beaches.desc: Where two seas meet — the Aegean and the Mediterranean — at a narrow sandy spit at the southernmost tip of Rhodes. World-class windsurfing.

beaches.name: Elli Beach
beaches.desc: The main town beach of Rhodes City — a long, well-organised beach right next to the old town. Very convenient.

restaurants.name: Marco Polo Café
restaurants.note: In a 15th-century Ottoman mansion in the old town. One of the most atmospheric restaurants in Rhodes.

restaurants.name: Mavrikos
restaurants.note: Family-run since 1933 — the best restaurant in Lindos. Book ahead, the terrace has stunning acropolis views.

restaurants.name: Pizanias
restaurants.note: Hidden in the medieval maze of the old town. Genuine Greek cooking at honest prices.

restaurants.name: Ta Kioupia
restaurants.note: In a beautiful garden setting. Considered one of the top restaurants in the whole of Rhodes.

restaurants.name: Alexis 4 Seasons
restaurants.note: Legendary seafood restaurant near the old town. Lobster and fresh fish prepared with precision.

restaurants.name: Nikos Takis
restaurants.note: The most creative menu in the old town. Beautiful presentation and excellent local wine selection.

restaurants.name: Philosophia
restaurants.note: Great mezze selection in a beautiful courtyard. Perfect for a long evening of small plates and wine.

restaurants.name: Elia
restaurants.note: Terrace restaurant with views over Lindos bay. Good food and a lovely setting.

restaurants.name: Fotis Melathron
restaurants.note: Reliable, authentic, and affordable. Good for a proper Greek meal without the tourist markup.

restaurants.name: Koykos
restaurants.note: Good fresh fish on the east coast. A reliable choice near the popular east coast beaches.

rentals.name: Multiple agencies (Rhodes airport & city)
rentals.desc: Essential for exploring beyond the city and east coast. The west coast and interior require a car.

rentals.name: Rent a Scooter Rhodes
rentals.desc: Great for the main tourist routes. Not recommended for the mountains or the far south.

rentals.name: Rhodes Boat Tours
rentals.desc: Day trips to Lindos by sea, Symi island, and the Turkish coast. Multiple operators from Mandraki harbour.

rentals.name: KTEL Rhodes
rentals.desc: Good bus network connecting the main towns and east coast beaches. Limited to the main routes.

accommodation.why: The most extraordinary place to stay — sleeping inside a UNESCO medieval city. Atmospheric boutique hotels in converted mansions.
The main resort strip west of the city. Good beaches, all-inclusive options, easy city access.
Staying in the village itself is magical — whitewashed captains houses, night views of the lit acropolis.
The main young/party resort on the east coast. Busy beaches, nightlife, watersports.

tips.title: Rhodes Old Town is unmissable
tips.text: Even if you are staying in a resort, spend at least one full day and evening wandering the medieval old town. It is extraordinary.

tips.title: July and August are extremely hot
tips.text: Rhodes can reach 38°C in peak summer. Visit ancient sites early morning. The beaches are still beautiful but crowded.

tips.title: Day trips to Symi are excellent
tips.text: The island of Symi (1.5 hours by fast boat) is one of the most beautiful in Greece. Day trips from Rhodes are very easy.

tips.title: Rhodes wine is underrated
tips.text: The local CAIR cooperative produces good white wines from the Athiri grape. Try a glass of local wine with your seafood.

tips.title: The south of the island is very different
tips.text: Drive to the south of Rhodes for a completely unspoilt, quiet, local experience. The tourist infrastructure is almost entirely in the north.

zakynthos.name: Zakynthos
zakynthos.description: Zakynthos — known in Italian as Zante — is the island that produced one of the most photographed images in the world: the rusting skeleton of a freighter stranded on a perfect white beach below soaring white cliffs. Beyond that iconic image, Zakynthos offers extraordinary natural beauty — sea caves of electric blue, the Venetian-influenced capital, a mountainous green interior, and the chance to witness loggerhead sea turtles nesting on the beach at night in one of Greece's most important wildlife sanctuaries.
zakynthos.funfact: Zakynthos hosts one of the largest loggerhead sea turtle (Caretta caretta) nesting sites in the Mediterranean — the turtles nest on Laganas beach every summer.

sights.name: Navagio (Shipwreck) Beach
sights.desc: The most photographed beach in Greece — a rusting shipwreck on white pebbles below towering white cliffs. Accessible only by boat. Arrive early to beat the day-tripper boats.

sights.name: Blue Caves
sights.desc: Electric-blue sea caves on the northern cape of the island where the water glows an impossible shade of azure. Best visited by small boat in the morning light.

sights.name: Sea Turtle Watching (Laganas)
sights.desc: Laganas Bay is one of the most important loggerhead turtle nesting sites in the Mediterranean. Night-time guided tours run June–August.

sights.name: Venetian Castle (Bochali)
sights.desc: The ruins of a Venetian fortress above the capital with panoramic views over the city and the Ionian Sea towards the Peloponnese.

sights.name: Keri Caves & Lighthouse
sights.desc: Sea caves and a lighthouse at the southernmost tip of the island. Dramatic cliffs, accessible by boat or road, with fantastic sunset views.

beaches.name: Navagio Beach
beaches.desc: The iconic shipwreck beach — white pebbles and brilliant turquoise water in an enclosed cove below massive white cliffs. Boat access only.

beaches.name: Gerakas Beach
beaches.desc: A long protected sandy beach that is also a protected loggerhead turtle nesting site. No sunbeds in the turtle zone. Beautiful and important.

beaches.name: Porto Zoro
beaches.desc: Fine golden sand, very clear water, pine trees above. One of the most beautiful accessible beaches on the island.

beaches.name: Xigia Beach
beaches.desc: A small beach with natural sulphur springs bubbling up through the sand — warm, slightly fizzy, and genuinely unusual.

beaches.name: Banana Beach
beaches.desc: Long sandy east coast beach — two separate stretches with watersports, sunbeds, and a lively beach bar scene.

restaurants.name: Malanos
restaurants.note: The most authentic Zakynthian cuisine in the capital. Slow-cooked stifado and rabbit dishes.

restaurants.name: Komis
restaurants.note: Excellent fresh fish on the east coast road. Family-run and genuinely good.

restaurants.name: Allegro
restaurants.note: The best evening restaurant in the capital. Great pasta and Ionian seafood combinations.

restaurants.name: Lofos Strani
restaurants.note: Below the Venetian castle with panoramic views over the town. Classic Greek food at good prices.

restaurants.name: Prosilio
restaurants.note: The most creative menu in the capital. Modern takes on Zakynthian classics with excellent wine.

restaurants.name: Dennis Restaurant
restaurants.note: A rural village taverna beloved by locals and visitors alike. Lamb on the spit on weekends.

restaurants.name: Ampelostrates
restaurants.note: In a vineyard setting. A wonderful combination of local wine, good food, and beautiful surroundings.

restaurants.name: Nobelos
restaurants.note: Clifftop restaurant on the north coast with extraordinary Ionian sea views. The most scenic table on the island.

restaurants.name: Zakanthi
restaurants.note: Modern Ionian cooking. Creative dishes that blend Greek tradition with contemporary technique.

restaurants.name: Mediterranean Beach Restaurant
restaurants.note: Reliable seafood on the busy Laganas beachfront. Good value for the location.

rentals.name: Multiple agencies (airport & Zakynthos Town)
rentals.desc: Essential for reaching Navagio viewpoint and the north of the island. The hilly roads require care.

rentals.name: Navagio & Blue Caves Boat Tours
rentals.desc: Essential — the iconic sights (Navagio beach, Blue Caves) are only accessible by sea. Multiple operators from Porto Vromi and Agios Nikolaos.

rentals.name: Zakynthos Moto Rentals
rentals.desc: Good for the main east coast route and around the capital. Not recommended for the steep northern roads.

rentals.name: KTEL Zakynthos
rentals.desc: Connects the main towns and some beaches. Infrequent outside peak season.

accommodation.why: The Venetian-influenced capital — most authentic, best restaurants, harbour promenade, and easy access for day trips everywhere.
The main resort area north of the capital. Sandy beach, watersports, lively bars, family-friendly.
The main party resort on the south coast. Busy beach, nightlife, close to the turtle nesting beach.
The most beautiful and natural area of the island — quiet, green, near Gerakas turtle beach. Perfect for a peaceful stay.

tips.title: Respect the sea turtle nesting zones
tips.text: The southern beaches (Laganas, Gerakas) are protected nesting sites. No sunbeds in marked zones, no noise or lights near the beach after dark during nesting season.

tips.title: Navagio is only accessible by boat
tips.text: The viewpoint from the clifftop gives the famous photo, but to actually reach the beach you need a boat from Porto Vromi or Agios Nikolaos (about €15 return).

tips.title: Try Zakynthian cuisine
tips.text: The Ionian islands have a distinct cuisine influenced by Venetian occupation — sofrito (beef in white wine sauce), bianco (fish stew), and mandolato nougat are all local.

tips.title: Navagio gets very crowded in peak season
tips.text: The beach fills with boats from 10am–3pm in July and August. Either get there very early by arranging a private boat, or go in the evening on a sunset tour.

tips.title: The Blue Caves are magnificent in the morning
tips.text: The light penetrates the water best between 9am and noon. Book a morning boat tour for the best electric-blue effect.

kefalonia.name: Kefalonia
kefalonia.description: Kefalonia is the largest and most dramatically beautiful of the Ionian Islands — a mountainous, wild, and deeply romantic island that inspired Captain Corelli's Mandolin and has been captivating visitors ever since. The beach of Myrtos is consistently voted one of the most beautiful in Europe, Melissani Lake is an underground cave lake where the midday sun creates electric-blue light through a hole in the roof, and the rugged interior has a grandeur that makes most other Greek islands feel tame by comparison.
kefalonia.funfact: Kefalonia's Mount Ainos (1,628m) is home to a unique species of Greek fir tree found nowhere else in the world — the Abies cephalonica, or Kefalonian fir.

sights.name: Myrtos Beach (Viewpoint & Beach)
sights.desc: Consistently voted one of the most beautiful beaches in Europe — a vertical descent to white pebbles and electric-blue water between giant limestone cliffs.

sights.name: Melissani Cave Lake
sights.desc: An underground lake inside a collapsed cave where sunlight through the roof opening creates an extraordinary electric-blue glow. One of the most magical natural sights in Greece.

sights.name: Assos Village
sights.desc: A tiny, perfectly preserved village on a narrow isthmus with a Venetian fortress above. One of the most beautiful villages in the Ionian Islands.

sights.name: Fiskardo
sights.desc: The only village that survived the 1953 earthquake — a charming harbour of Venetian-era buildings, boutique shops, and excellent restaurants. The most chic village in Kefalonia.

sights.name: Mount Ainos National Park
sights.desc: The forested mountain interior of Kefalonia — wild horses, ancient fir trees, and panoramic views. A complete contrast to the beach scene.

beaches.name: Myrtos
beaches.desc: Widely regarded as one of the most beautiful beaches in Europe. White pebbles, electric-blue water, dramatic white cliffs. Steep access road, no shade, worth every bit of it.

beaches.name: Antisamos
beaches.desc: A beautiful pebble beach near Sami surrounded by green hills. Used as a filming location for Captain Corelli's Mandolin. Very clear water.

beaches.name: Makris Gialos
beaches.desc: Long organised beach near Lassi with fine sand, calm water, and good facilities. The most practical beach near the capital.

beaches.name: Xi Beach
beaches.desc: A unique beach of fine red-orange sand (from natural clay deposits) on the south coast. Unusual colour and very calm water.

beaches.name: Lourdas
beaches.desc: A long crescent of sandy beach backed by olive groves and the green Ainos foothills. Beautiful, less crowded than the north. Good tavernas.

restaurants.name: Tassia
restaurants.note: The legendary restaurant of Fiskardo, run by Tassia Dendrinou since 1979. Cookbook author and culinary institution. Book well ahead.

restaurants.name: Patsouras
restaurants.pexels_q: traditional Greek Ionian food meat stew
restaurants.note: The most authentic Kefalonian kitchen in the capital. Slow-cooked meat dishes and local wine.

restaurants.name: El Greco
restaurants.note: Charming harbour-side terrace in Fiskardo. Good fish and pasta with a lovely view of the yachts.

restaurants.name: Platanos
restaurants.pexels_q: Greek taverna under plane tree village
restaurants.note: Under a giant plane tree in the most beautiful village square in Kefalonia. Simple, delicious, perfect.

restaurants.name: Casa Grec
restaurants.note: The best modern restaurant in the capital. Creative Kefalonian cooking with a great wine list.

restaurants.name: Aquarius
restaurants.note: Right on Lourdas beach. Fresh fish, grilled octopus, cold white wine with the beach right in front.

restaurants.name: Patsavouras
restaurants.note: A classic Argostoli ouzo bar serving excellent mezze. Sit outside and watch the waterfront.

restaurants.name: Alexis
restaurants.note: Reliable seafood in the port town of Sami, convenient if you are visiting Melissani.

restaurants.name: Vineleaf
restaurants.note: Good food in a lovely garden setting near the Fiskardo harbour. Good wine list.

restaurants.name: Ladokola
restaurants.note: The best souvlaki in the capital. Simple, cheap, and genuinely delicious.

rentals.name: Multiple agencies (Kefalonia airport & Argostoli)
rentals.desc: Essential for Kefalonia. The island is mountainous and large — many sights are only reachable by car. Book ahead.

rentals.name: Kefalonia Boat Hire (Fiskardo & Argostoli)
rentals.desc: Charter a small boat to explore the sea caves, swim at Myrtos from the water, and visit Ithaca for the day.

rentals.name: Kefalonia Moto Rent
rentals.desc: Good for coastal routes and around the capital. The mountain roads to Myrtos and Assos are not suitable for scooters.

rentals.name: Kefalonia Nature Walks
rentals.desc: Guided hikes through the Ainos National Park and along the coastal paths. Expert local guides.

accommodation.why: The most beautiful and chic village — Venetian harbour, excellent restaurants, boutique hotels. The most romantic base on the island.
Tiny, breathtaking village on a peninsula below a castle. A handful of small hotels and a handful of perfect evenings.
The capital — most practical base for the whole island. Good restaurants, car hire, and the main ferry port.
Resort area near the capital — organised beaches, hotels, watersports. Most convenient for families.

tips.title: Myrtos Beach requires an early start
tips.text: Myrtos fills up by 11am in peak season and the car park overflows. Arrive before 9am, or visit in the late afternoon when the crowds thin.

tips.title: Kefalonia sits on a major fault line
tips.text: The devastating earthquake of 1953 destroyed almost every building on the island. Fiskardo is the rare exception. The rebuilt capital and towns have a 1950s feel as a result.

tips.title: Robola wine is world-class
tips.text: Kefalonia produces Robola, a crisp dry white wine from vines grown at altitude. It is one of Greece's finest wines and pairs perfectly with Ionian seafood.

tips.title: Captain Corelli's Mandolin country
tips.text: Louis de Bernières set his famous novel here. Visiting Sami and Fiskardo with the book in mind adds a wonderful extra dimension to the trip.

tips.title: Mountain roads are beautiful but demanding
tips.text: The road to Myrtos and Assos involves serious hairpin bends and sheer drops. Take your time and enjoy the views at the designated viewpoints.

thassos.name: Thassos
thassos.tagline: Green forests, marble & the clearest northern waters
thassos.description: Thassos is a revelation for those who discover it — a densely forested island of white marble and crystal-clear water in the northern Aegean, close enough to the mainland to reach by a 35-minute ferry from Kavala. The island is spectacularly green — pine forests cover the mountains all the way to the sea, marble-paved villages cling to hillsides, and waterfalls cascade through ancient forests. It lacks the dramatic volcanic formations of the Cyclades but more than makes up for it with lush scenery, family-friendly beaches with shallow turquoise water, and a genuine, unhurried local life.
thassos.funfact: Thassos has been quarried for white marble since antiquity — the same marble used to build monuments in ancient Athens. The marble is still commercially quarried today.

sights.name: Ancient Thassos (Limenas)
sights.desc: Remarkable ancient ruins right in the main town — an agora, theatre, temples, and a circuit of ancient walls with towers. One of the best ancient sites in northern Greece.

sights.name: Alyki Archaeological Site
sights.desc: A magical double cove with ancient marble quarries and ruins right on the beach. You swim in crystal-clear water surrounded by 2,500-year-old carved stone.

sights.name: Giola Natural Pool
sights.desc: A natural rock pool connected to the sea by an underwater channel — perfectly clear warm water in a dramatic rock formation at the southern tip of the island.

sights.name: Theological School of Athos (Theologos)
sights.desc: The most beautiful and best-preserved inland village on Thassos — a mountain village of stone houses, churches, and magnificent views, with excellent local tavernas.

sights.name: Limenaria
sights.desc: A charming southern port town with an atmospheric old quarter, a ruined German mine administrator's mansion above the harbour, and excellent fresh fish restaurants.

beaches.name: Paradise Beach
beaches.desc: Fine golden sand, shallow crystal-clear water, and pine trees right to the beach. Consistently voted one of the best beaches in northern Greece.

beaches.name: Golden Beach (Skala Panagia)
beaches.desc: The longest beach on the island — 1.5km of fine golden sand with calm, shallow water. Organised sunbeds and excellent tavernas.

beaches.name: Marble Beach (Saliara)
beaches.desc: A beach of brilliant white marble pebbles — dazzling in the sun. Only accessible by boat or a short hike. Extraordinarily beautiful.

beaches.name: Alyki
beaches.desc: Twin coves at the ancient archaeological site. Clear water, white marble rock, pine trees. One of the most beautiful spots on the island.

beaches.name: Pachys Ammos
beaches.desc: Secluded beach accessible by a short hike through pine forest. Fine sand, very clear water, and few visitors. The most peaceful beach on Thassos.

restaurants.name: Symposium
restaurants.pexels_q: Greek traditional taverna sea view food
restaurants.note: The best traditional restaurant in the main town. Generous portions of authentic Greek food.

restaurants.name: To Karnagio
restaurants.pexels_q: Greek harbour seafood grilled fish fresh
restaurants.note: On the harbour in Limenas. Fresh fish direct from local fishermen. Outstanding grilled sea bass.

restaurants.name: Plateia
restaurants.pexels_q: Greek mountain village goat food traditional
restaurants.note: In the beautiful mountain village of Theologos. Goat, lamb, and local sausages cooked over wood fire.

restaurants.name: Ta Limenia
restaurants.note: Excellent mezze and seafood in the charming port of Limenaria. Good value and generous portions.

restaurants.name: Gorgona
restaurants.note: Right on Golden Beach. Good for a beach lunch — fresh fish, salads, cold beer.

restaurants.name: The Olive Press
restaurants.note: In a converted olive press. Atmospheric rustic setting with good Mediterranean food.

restaurants.name: Akrogiali
restaurants.pexels_q: Greek seaside taverna fresh fish octopus
restaurants.note: Harbourfront taverna in Potos. Reliable fresh seafood and good local wine.

restaurants.name: Tarsanas
restaurants.note: A local favourite in the main town. Good moussaka, pastitsio, and grilled meats.

restaurants.name: Zorbas
restaurants.note: Simple, honest Greek food near the Kavala ferry port. Good value for money.

restaurants.name: Amfipoli
restaurants.note: Good all-round taverna in the main town. Reliable food and cold Mythos beer.

rentals.name: Multiple agencies (Limenas & ferry ports)
rentals.desc: A car lets you circle the entire island in a day. The coastal road is spectacular — pine forests, marble beaches, fishing villages.

rentals.name: Thassos Bike Rentals
rentals.desc: Perfect for the flat coastal route around the island. Some inland roads are steep and better suited to cars.

rentals.name: Thassos Boat Trips
rentals.desc: Half-day tours visiting Marble Beach, sea caves, and the uninhabited islets around the island.

rentals.name: KTEL Thassos
rentals.desc: A bus route circles the island. Cheap but infrequent — useful for getting between main towns.

accommodation.why: The main town with the ancient ruins, harbour, and best restaurants. The most convenient and interesting base.
Right by the longest and most popular beach. Great for families wanting easy beach access.
Beautiful beach village on the east coast. Charming, relatively quiet, good tavernas.
Southern resort area — organised beaches, good facilities, lively in summer, calmer than the north.

tips.title: Thassos is exceptional value
tips.text: Compared to the Cyclades or Dodecanese, Thassos is significantly cheaper across hotels, restaurants, and activities. You get more for your money here than almost anywhere in Greece.

tips.title: Easy to reach from the mainland
tips.text: The ferry from Kavala to Limenas takes just 35 minutes and runs very frequently. A great option if you are already planning to visit northern Greece or Thessaloniki.

tips.title: The forested interior is extraordinary
tips.text: Unlike most Greek islands, Thassos has dense pine and oak forests covering its mountains. The drive through the interior to Theologos village is stunning.

tips.title: Northern Aegean is cooler than the south
tips.text: The sea around Thassos is cooler than the Cyclades or Dodecanese — particularly in June and September. Still perfectly swimmable, but noticeably fresher.

tips.title: Local honey and chestnuts are excellent
tips.text: The pine forests produce distinctive honey, and the chestnut trees in the mountains produce chestnuts in autumn. Buy both at the local markets in Theologos and Prinos.

corsica.name: Corsica
corsica.description: Corsica is unlike any other Mediterranean island — a mountain range surrounded by sea. The interior is wild and almost Alpine: pine forests, granite peaks, and ancient Genoese towers on every headland. Drive 20 minutes and you're on a beach with water so clear it looks photoshopped. The island has a fierce, proud identity (Napoleon was born here) and a cuisine of mountain traditions — chestnut flour, wild mint honey, aged sheep's cheeses, and charcuterie that puts the rest of Europe to shame.
corsica.ferry: Nice → Ajaccio (~5.5 hrs) / Marseille → Ajaccio (~10 hrs)
corsica.funfact: Napoleon Bonaparte was born in Ajaccio, Corsica in 1769 — just a year after France purchased the island from Genoa.

sights.name: Bonifacio
sights.desc: A medieval citadel town perched on white limestone cliffs above a turquoise inlet. One of the most dramatically positioned towns in all of Europe.

sights.name: Les Calanques de Piana
sights.desc: UNESCO-listed pink granite rock formations rising from the sea near Porto. Drive the coast road at sunset for maximum drama.

sights.name: GR20 Trail
sights.desc: Considered the toughest long-distance trail in Europe — 180km through granite mountains. Even a day section rewards with extraordinary scenery.

sights.name: Corte & the Interior
sights.desc: The mountain capital and soul of Corsica. Ancient citadel, gorge walks, and the most authentic Corsican food.

sights.name: Genoese Towers
sights.desc: Corsica has 85 Genoese watchtowers built to protect against pirate raids. Many are accessible and offer magnificent coastal views.

beaches.name: Palombaggia
beaches.desc: Often listed among the best beaches in Europe — fine pale sand, turquoise water, and a backdrop of umbrella pines near Porto-Vecchio.

beaches.name: Rondinara
beaches.desc: A perfect circular cove with shallow, crystal-clear water. A short walk from a small car park.

beaches.name: Saleccia
beaches.desc: Wild, undeveloped beach in the Agriates desert. Accessible only by 4x4 track or boat. The most beautiful unspoilt beach in Corsica.

beaches.name: Santa Giulia
beaches.desc: Calm, sheltered lagoon beach ideal for families. Clear turquoise water, watersports, good facilities near Porto-Vecchio.

beaches.name: Arone
beaches.desc: Remote beach in the far west near the Calanques. Dramatic volcanic rock backdrop, very clear water, far fewer visitors.

restaurants.name: A Pignata
restaurants.pexels_q: Corsican mountain stew wild boar chestnut
restaurants.note: In a remote village in the Alta Rocca. Legendary slow-cooked stews, wild boar, chestnut dishes.

restaurants.name: Le Voilier
restaurants.note: On the marina below the clifftop citadel. Exceptional fresh fish and Corsican charcuterie boards.

restaurants.name: Chez Madeleine
restaurants.note: The most beloved lunch spot in the interior. Chestnut soup, figatellu sausage, brocciu cheese.

restaurants.name: La Signoria
restaurants.note: In a beautiful estate hotel. The island's most refined dining — Corsican ingredients elevated to haute cuisine.

restaurants.name: Le Belvédère
restaurants.note: Perched above the Gulf of Porto with spectacular views over the Calanques.

restaurants.name: A Mandria di Pigna
restaurants.pexels_q: Corsican artisan food cheese jam wine
restaurants.note: In Corsica's famous craft village. Local cheeses, homemade jams, and Corsican wine.

restaurants.name: U Capu Biancu
restaurants.pexels_q: luxury cliff top Mediterranean dining sea view
restaurants.note: Hotel restaurant on a spectacular clifftop south of Bonifacio. The view over the Sardinian strait is as good as the food.

restaurants.name: A Nepita
restaurants.pexels_q: creative French Corsican cuisine fine dining
restaurants.note: The best restaurant in the capital. Creative cooking — the chef updates the menu daily based on seasonal produce.

restaurants.name: Chez Toinou
restaurants.note: Long-established local favourite near the best southern beaches. Great charcuterie and good value.

restaurants.name: La Table de la Ferme
restaurants.pexels_q: farm to table Corsican countryside food
restaurants.note: On a working Corsican farm. Everything on the table is produced here — cheese, charcuterie, honey. Pre-book only.

rentals.name: Avis / Europcar (airports & ports)
rentals.desc: Essential for Corsica. The road network is excellent on the coast, challenging in the mountains.

rentals.name: Local 4x4 rentals (Porto-Vecchio)
rentals.desc: For accessing Saleccia beach, the Agriates desert, and mountain villages. Opens up a different Corsica.

rentals.name: Corsica Croisières
rentals.desc: Day trips to Scandola Nature Reserve (UNESCO, no road access), Girolata, and the Calanques by sea.

rentals.name: In Corsica Guides
rentals.desc: Guided day hikes and multi-day treks. GR20 sections, gorge walks, summit routes.

accommodation.why: The most dramatic and beautiful town in Corsica. Clifftop citadel, excellent restaurants, close to the best southern beaches.
The most elegant resort town — a Genoese citadel, a long sandy beach, and a lively marina.
Most popular base for southern beach exploration. Good facilities and excellent restaurants.
The mountain capital — for those who want the real Corsica. Gorge walks, ancient citadel, much cheaper.

tips.title: Forest fire risk is very high in summer
tips.text: Corsica's forests are extremely dry in July–August. Barbecuing outside official sites is illegal and dangerous.

tips.title: Buy Corsican products — they are exceptional
tips.text: Chestnut honey, figatellu sausage, brocciu cheese, Pietra beer, and Nielluccio wine are world-class. Visit a village market.

tips.title: Mountain road driving requires confidence
tips.text: The D81 coast road near the Calanques has narrow sections with steep drops. Take your time.

tips.title: Mistral and Tramontane winds can close beaches
tips.text: Northwest winds can be violent and make some north-coast beaches dangerous with little warning.

tips.title: The maquis fragrance is part of the experience
tips.text: Corsica's scrubland of rosemary, lavender, and myrtle gives the island a distinctive perfume. Napoleon said he could identify Corsica blindfolded.

sardinia.name: Sardinia
sardinia.description: Sardinia is the Mediterranean at its most ancient and unspoilt. The second-largest island has been inhabited for over 8,000 years, and 7,000 mysterious nuraghe stone towers dot the landscape with no parallel anywhere on earth. Above ground: the Costa Smeralda's jewel-like coves, the wild flamingo lagoons of the south, and the chalk-white sea stacks of the Orosei coast accessible only by boat. Sardinian food is as ancient as the landscape — roast suckling pig, pane carasau flatbread, Cannonau wine, and bottarga (cured mullet roe).
sardinia.ferry: Genoa → Cagliari (~20 hrs) / Rome Civitavecchia → Olbia (~8 hrs)
sardinia.funfact: Sardinia's mountainous Barbagia region is one of only five 'Blue Zones' on earth where people routinely live past 100.

sights.name: Nuraghe Su Nuraxi
sights.desc: Sardinia's most impressive Bronze Age tower — a UNESCO World Heritage Site from 1500 BC. One of the most mysterious ancient monuments in Europe.

sights.name: Costa Smeralda
sights.desc: The legendary northeastern coastline where the Aga Khan built the most exclusive resort in the Mediterranean. The water colour is genuinely extraordinary.

sights.name: Alghero Old Town
sights.desc: A Catalan-influenced medieval city on the northwest coast. The most charming town in Sardinia — excellent for an evening passeggiata above the sea.

sights.name: Cala Gonone Boat Tour
sights.desc: The only way to access the most spectacular coves on the Orosei coast — Cala Luna, Cala Mariolu, and the Grotta del Bue Marino.

sights.name: Cagliari Castello
sights.desc: The medieval hilltop citadel of the capital. Panoramic terraces, a cathedral, Roman amphitheatre, and the best food market in Sardinia at the base.

beaches.name: Cala Mariolu
beaches.desc: Often cited as the most beautiful beach in Italy — white pebbles and water of extraordinary clarity. Boat access only from Cala Gonone.

beaches.name: La Pelosa
beaches.desc: Shallow Caribbean-blue lagoon near Stintino with white sand and views of a Genoese tower. Now requires a timed entry ticket in high season.

beaches.name: Cala Goloritzè
beaches.desc: A UNESCO site — accessible by 3km mountain trail or boat. A dramatic rock arch over a turquoise cove.

beaches.name: Spiaggia del Principe
beaches.desc: In the heart of Costa Smeralda — fine white sand, granite rocks, and water in remarkable shades of green and blue.

beaches.name: Is Arutas
beaches.desc: An unusual beach of white quartz crystals that shimmer in the sun — the grains look like grains of rice. A completely unique texture.

restaurants.name: La Lepanto
restaurants.note: The most celebrated restaurant in Alghero. The aragosta (spiny lobster) in Catalan style is a Sardinian institution.

restaurants.name: Ristorante Gino
restaurants.note: Best restaurant in Cala Gonone. Fresh catch from the Orosei gulf, exceptional bottarga pasta.

restaurants.name: Il Rifugio
restaurants.pexels_q: Sardinian porceddu roast pig mountain food
restaurants.note: The definitive Sardinian mountain meal: porceddu (roast suckling pig), culurgiones, and Cannonau wine.

restaurants.name: Il Corsaro
restaurants.note: The most refined restaurant in the capital. Creative modern Sardinian cooking with an exceptional wine cellar.

restaurants.name: Sabores de Olia
restaurants.note: In a Barbagia mountain village (a Blue Zone). Everything handmade. The ravioli and lamb are extraordinary.

restaurants.name: La Bitta
restaurants.note: The most atmospheric restaurant in the Costa Smeralda. Romantic garden dining with full glamour.

restaurants.name: Dal Corsaro
restaurants.note: Long-established fine dining in the capital. The pasta with bottarga is outstanding.

restaurants.name: Trattoria Lillicu
restaurants.note: Honest family trattoria serving Cagliari classics since 1968. Bottarga, malloreddus, and grilled sea bream.

restaurants.name: Agriturismo Deriu
restaurants.note: A working sheep farm serving a fixed menu of everything they produce. Book ahead.

restaurants.name: Ristorante Faro
restaurants.pexels_q: lighthouse seafood restaurant sea view Sardinia
restaurants.note: By a lighthouse on the cape west of Alghero. Fresh grilled fish, cold Vermentino, extraordinary views.

rentals.name: Avis / Hertz (Cagliari, Olbia, Alghero)
rentals.desc: Essential for exploring Sardinia properly. Rent for your entire trip.

rentals.name: Cala Gonone Boat Tours
rentals.desc: Essential — the most spectacular beaches (Cala Mariolu, Cala Goloritzè) are only accessible by boat.

rentals.name: Barbagia Jeep Tours
rentals.desc: Guided 4x4 tours into the Gennargentu mountains and Barbagia villages.

rentals.name: Sardinia Bike (multiple locations)
rentals.desc: E-bike rentals for coastal routes near Alghero, Oristano, and Villasimius.

accommodation.why: The most characterful town. Medieval walls, excellent restaurants, good beach nearby.
Base for the spectacular Orosei coast boat trips. Small, authentic, excellent seafood.
The most exclusive address in the Mediterranean. Superyachts, designer boutiques, extraordinary water.
The lively capital — best for food, culture, and nightlife. Good base for southern beaches.

tips.title: Never remove sand or pebbles from beaches
tips.text: It is illegal to remove sand, pebbles, or shells from Sardinian beaches. Fines of up to €3,000 apply.

tips.title: Book La Pelosa entry tickets in advance
tips.text: La Pelosa near Stintino requires timed entry tickets in July and August. Book online before you arrive.

tips.title: Cannonau wine is exceptional and healthy
tips.text: Sardinia's Cannonau red is one of the highest in polyphenols of any wine — which locals credit for their extraordinary longevity.

tips.title: Mosquitoes can be serious in wetland areas
tips.text: Near Oristano and the flamingo lagoons, mosquito activity can be intense at dawn and dusk. Bring repellent.

tips.title: The Orosei coast is best seen by boat
tips.text: Book your Cala Gonone boat tour for the first or second day — they fill up quickly in season.

sicily.name: Sicily
sicily.description: Sicily is the crossroads of the Mediterranean — every civilisation that ever mattered has left its mark here. From the Greeks who built Agrigento's temples in 500 BC to the Arabs who gave Palermo its souk-like markets, to the Normans who created the most extraordinary fusion of Christian and Islamic architecture in the world. It is also the foot of one of Europe's most active volcanoes. The food is extraordinary: arancini, cannoli, pasta alla Norma, and swordfish preparations that have barely changed since the Arab occupation.
sicily.ferry: Naples → Palermo (~11 hrs) / Reggio Calabria → Messina (15 mins)
sicily.funfact: The Valley of the Temples at Agrigento contains seven Greek temples from the 5th century BC — some better preserved than anything on mainland Greece.
hero_queries: Scala dei Turchi white cliffs Sicily

sights.name: Valley of the Temples
sights.desc: Seven remarkably preserved Greek temples from the 5th century BC near Agrigento. UNESCO World Heritage Site — more intact than anything in Greece itself.

sights.name: Taormina
sights.desc: The most beautiful hill town in Sicily — a Baroque jewel above the Ionian Sea with a 3rd-century BC Greek theatre still hosting live performances with Etna as a backdrop.

sights.name: Mount Etna
sights.desc: Europe's largest active volcano. Cable car and guided walks reach the summit craters at 3,329m. The moonscape of dried lava flows is extraordinary.

sights.name: Palermo Historic Centre
sights.desc: Norman-Arab-Byzantine architecture, Baroque palaces, and the wildest street food markets in Italy — all within walking distance.

sights.name: Syracuse & Ortigia Island
sights.desc: The ancient Greek city that was once the rival of Athens. Ortigia has a Baroque waterfront, a Greek temple converted into a cathedral, and excellent fish restaurants.

beaches.name: San Vito lo Capo
beaches.desc: The most beautiful beach in western Sicily — a long arc of fine white sand and crystal-clear water with the Zingaro nature reserve as a backdrop.

beaches.name: Scala dei Turchi
beaches.desc: Dazzling white terraced cliffs of marl limestone descending to a clear sea near Agrigento. One of the most unusual natural formations in Sicily.

beaches.name: Isola Bella (Taormina)
beaches.desc: A tiny island connected to the Taormina coast by a narrow sandbar — turquoise coves on both sides with the town and Etna above.

beaches.name: Cefalù Beach
beaches.desc: A beautiful town beach below a Norman cathedral and a dramatic rock. Good swimming, easy access, picturesque setting.

beaches.name: Riserva dello Zingaro
beaches.desc: Sicily's first nature reserve — secluded coves accessible only on foot along a 7km coastal trail. Pristine, no cars, no facilities.

restaurants.name: Ristorante La Madia
restaurants.note: Two Michelin stars. Chef Pino Cuttaia transforms Sicilian street food into extraordinary high cuisine.

restaurants.name: Osteria dei Vespri
restaurants.pexels_q: modern Sicilian Italian cuisine elegant dining
restaurants.note: In a 17th-century Baroque palace in central Palermo. Elegant, creative Sicilian cooking.

restaurants.name: Duomo
restaurants.note: Two Michelin stars in the most beautiful Baroque town in Sicily. Worth the trip to Ragusa alone.

restaurants.name: Ferro di Cavallo
restaurants.note: An institution since 1944. The most authentic and affordable Palermitan meal you will find.

restaurants.name: Ristorante Don Camillo
restaurants.note: In Ortigia — the best restaurant in Syracuse. Spectacular pasta with sea urchin.

restaurants.name: Trattoria da Benito
restaurants.note: The antidote to touristy Taormina. Pasta con le sarde and swordfish involtini — the real thing.

restaurants.name: La Brace
restaurants.note: The go-to for honest Catanese cooking near Etna. Pasta alla Norma with local aubergines is outstanding.

restaurants.name: Majore
restaurants.note: The best pork restaurant in Sicily. The extraordinary black pigs here are famous across Italy.

restaurants.name: Ristorante Cialoma
restaurants.note: In a beautiful fishing village in the deep south. Bluefin tuna prepared every way.

restaurants.name: Nangarell
restaurants.note: The best restaurant near the Valley of the Temples. Great almond-based desserts.

rentals.name: Avis / Hertz (Palermo, Catania airports)
rentals.desc: Essential for Sicily. The Valley of the Temples, Zingaro, and the interior are only reachable by car.

rentals.name: Liberty Lines & Siremar (Milazzo)
rentals.desc: Hydrofoil and ferry services to all seven Aeolian Islands. Stromboli's active volcano is unmissable.

rentals.name: Etna Experience
rentals.desc: Guided ascents of Etna with a volcanologist guide. Cable car to 2,500m then walk to the summit craters.

rentals.name: Local rentals (Palermo, Catania, Taormina)
rentals.desc: Best for exploring individual towns and their surroundings.

accommodation.why: The most beautiful and atmospheric town. Greek theatre, Etna views, excellent restaurants, beach access.
The most fascinating city — extraordinary architecture, best street food in Italy, vibrant energy.
Staying on Ortigia island is one of the great Mediterranean experiences — Baroque waterfront, excellent fish.
The most extraordinary Baroque town in Sicily — a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Remote but unforgettable.

tips.title: July and August are brutally hot
tips.text: Sicily in peak summer can reach 42°C. Visit ancient sites early morning. April–June or September–October are far better.

tips.title: Eat everything — the food is extraordinary
tips.text: From street arancini at dawn in Palermo to a cannolo from Piana degli Albanesi, every meal is a cultural experience.

tips.title: Driving in Palermo requires nerves
tips.text: Palermo traffic operates on unwritten rules. Park at the edge and walk or taxi.

tips.title: Book top restaurants months ahead
tips.text: The best Etna guided tours and Michelin-starred restaurants book out months in advance in high season.

tips.title: See a performance at the Greek Theatre in Taormina
tips.text: Seeing music in a 2,300-year-old Greek theatre with Etna behind the stage is one of the great Mediterranean experiences.

mallorca.name: Mallorca
mallorca.tagline: Dramatic cliffs, hidden coves & Baroque palaces
mallorca.description: Mallorca is a far more sophisticated island than its package-holiday reputation suggests. The northwest coast, protected by the Serra de Tramuntana mountain range (a UNESCO World Heritage Site), is one of the most dramatic coastal landscapes in the Mediterranean. Palma de Mallorca is genuinely one of Europe's most beautiful cities, with a Gothic cathedral rising above the sea and Renaissance palaces converted into boutique hotels. Rent a car, take the vintage wooden train to Sóller, and discover that the real Mallorca has very little in common with the Magaluf strip.
mallorca.ferry: Barcelona → Palma (~8 hrs) / Valencia → Palma (~6 hrs)
mallorca.funfact: The Serra de Tramuntana was added to the UNESCO World Heritage List in 2011 — the only cultural landscape on a Mediterranean island to receive this designation.

sights.name: Palma Cathedral (La Seu)
sights.desc: One of the greatest Gothic cathedrals in Europe, built over 400 years and overlooking the sea. The rose window — 12 metres in diameter — is extraordinary.

sights.name: Valldemossa Monastery
sights.desc: A honey-coloured stone village in the Tramuntana mountains where Chopin and George Sand spent the winter of 1838–39. The monastery where they stayed is the main sight.

sights.name: Sa Calobra
sights.desc: The most dramatic drive in the Balearics — 13km of 270° hairpin bends descending to a turquoise cove hemmed in by 200m limestone cliffs.

sights.name: Cap de Formentor
sights.desc: A long, narrow peninsula of wild cliffs and pine forests culminating in a lighthouse 200m above the sea. Extraordinary views over the bay of Pollença.

sights.name: Palma Old Town
sights.desc: Beyond the cathedral, Palma has a Renaissance old town of extraordinary quality — Arab baths, medieval palaces, and a contemporary art scene.

beaches.name: Cala Mondragó
beaches.desc: A protected natural park beach — pine-fringed, clear water, fine sand, no large hotels allowed. One of the most beautiful and best-preserved beaches on the island.

beaches.name: Platja de Muro
beaches.desc: A long, wide beach of fine white sand on the sheltered Bay of Alcúdia. Calm water, good facilities — ideal for families.

beaches.name: Cala Deià
beaches.desc: A tiny rocky cove below the village of Deià in the Tramuntana. Swim in clear turquoise water off the rocks and eat at the beach bar.

beaches.name: Sa Calobra
beaches.desc: At the bottom of the famous hairpin road — a narrow gorge opens onto a shingle beach of extraordinary turquoise water.

beaches.name: Cala Llombards
beaches.desc: A small, sheltered cove in the southeast between pine-covered rocky headlands. One of the most unspoilt small beaches in Mallorca.

restaurants.name: Marc Fosh
restaurants.note: One Michelin star. The best restaurant in Palma. British chef Marc Fosh uses Mallorcan produce in elegant dishes.

restaurants.name: Ca Na Toneta
restaurants.pexels_q: traditional Mallorcan food slow food local
restaurants.note: The most celebrated traditional restaurant. Two sisters cooking slow-food Mallorcan cuisine. Book weeks ahead.

restaurants.name: Es Fum
restaurants.pexels_q: Mallorca fine dining sea view Michelin
restaurants.note: One Michelin star. Contemporary cooking in an extraordinary clifftop setting with panoramic sea views.

restaurants.name: Béns d'Avall
restaurants.note: Perched on a cliff between Sóller and Deià. Extraordinary views and beautifully crafted Mediterranean dishes.

restaurants.name: La Fortaleza
restaurants.note: In a 16th-century fortress above the bay of Pollença. Extraordinary setting with excellent local cooking.

restaurants.name: Simply Fosh
restaurants.note: Marc Fosh's more casual sister restaurant — excellent value in the same beautiful Renaissance courtyard.

restaurants.name: Es Cantonet
restaurants.note: The village restaurant locals love. Honest sobrassada, tumbet, and grilled fish at fair prices.

restaurants.name: Sa Cova
restaurants.note: On the waterfront of the most charming port town. Fresh fish, prawns, and caldereta with panoramic bay views.

restaurants.name: Celler Sa Premsa
restaurants.pexels_q: classic Mallorcan food lechona roast pig
restaurants.note: A genuine old Palma wine cellar serving traditional Mallorcan food since 1958. The lechona is outstanding.

restaurants.name: Restaurant Mandala
restaurants.note: In the most beautiful village in Mallorca. Terrace dining with mountain and sea views.

rentals.name: Avis / Europcar (Palma airport)
rentals.desc: Essential for the Tramuntana mountains and southeastern coves. Book in advance for July and August.

rentals.name: Mallorca Cycling (multiple)
rentals.desc: Mallorca is the cycling capital of Europe. Hundreds of kilometres of marked routes.

rentals.name: Click&Boat Mallorca
rentals.desc: Day boat charters to explore hidden coves inaccessible by road, especially the Tramuntana coast.

rentals.name: Ferrocarrils de Mallorca
rentals.desc: The vintage wooden train from Palma to Sóller (1912) is one of the great short train journeys in Europe.

accommodation.why: The finest city in the Balearics — Gothic cathedral, Renaissance palaces, excellent restaurants and nightlife.
The most beautiful village — a UNESCO-protected mountain village above the sea with the best restaurants.
Elegant northern resort town with a long sandy bay, a beautiful promenade, and easy access to Formentor.
The southeast — near the best-preserved coves and the most authentic village life.

tips.title: Avoid Magaluf and the south resort strip
tips.text: The strip from Arenal to Magaluf is mass-market package tourism. The real Mallorca is the northwest, Palma, and the southeast.

tips.title: Take the wooden train to Sóller
tips.text: The vintage train from Palma to Sóller (1912) through the Tramuntana is genuinely one of the great short train journeys in Europe.

tips.title: Sa Calobra road requires a confident driver
tips.text: The 13km descent has 270° bends and coaches coming the other way. Alternatively, arrive by boat from Port de Sóller.

tips.title: August is very busy — book far ahead
tips.text: Mallorca in August is packed. Hotels, restaurants, and boat trips book out months in advance.

tips.title: Cycling in Mallorca is world-class
tips.text: Professional cycling teams train here every February–March. The Tramuntana climbs are legendary.

ibiza.name: Ibiza
ibiza.description: Ibiza has two very distinct personalities. There is the island of legendary nightlife — the clubs that have defined electronic music culture for 40 years, the sunset sessions at Café del Mar — and then there is the other Ibiza: a UNESCO World Heritage old town, 50 kilometres of coastline dotted with pine-fringed coves of extraordinary clarity, a thriving organic food scene, and an interior of almond orchards and ancient fincas. The genius of the island is that both versions are authentic and simultaneously available.
ibiza.ferry: Barcelona → Ibiza (~9 hrs) / Valencia → Ibiza (~6 hrs)
ibiza.funfact: Ibiza Town's old city (Dalt Vila) was added to the UNESCO World Heritage List in 1999 — one of only a handful of entire fortified towns in the world to receive this designation.
hero_queries: Ibiza Town Dalt Vila fortress sunset

sights.name: Dalt Vila (Ibiza Town)
sights.desc: A UNESCO World Heritage fortified old town — a maze of whitewashed Moorish streets, Renaissance walls, and a cathedral with extraordinary views.

sights.name: Es Vedrà
sights.desc: A dramatic uninhabited limestone rock rising 413m from the sea. Associated with dozens of legends. The most powerful natural sight on the island.

sights.name: Café del Mar Sunset
sights.desc: The legendary sunset bar at Sant Antoni that invented the concept of the sunset session in 1980. Ambient music, golden light — a genuine cultural institution.

sights.name: Las Dalias Hippie Market
sights.desc: The most famous market in Ibiza — running every Saturday since 1954. Artisan jewellery, organic food, and live music in a beautiful garden.

sights.name: Santa Inés Almond Blossom
sights.desc: In late January and February, the almond trees of the northwest interior turn white with blossom. The most beautiful and least-known seasonal sight.

beaches.name: Cala Conta
beaches.desc: Two coves of extraordinary turquoise water with views of Es Vedrà at sunset. The most beautiful beach-and-view combination in Ibiza.

beaches.name: Ses Salines
beaches.desc: A long beach backed by a natural park of salt lakes and flamingos. Beautiful water, good restaurants, and a fashionable crowd.

beaches.name: Cala Xarraca
beaches.desc: A quiet, sheltered cove in the north with very clear, calm water. Pine trees reach to the water's edge. The most peaceful swimming beach.

beaches.name: Playa d'en Bossa
beaches.desc: The longest beach on the island and the epicentre of the club beach scene. Ushuaïa and Hi Ibiza are both here.

beaches.name: Cala Jondal
beaches.desc: A fashionable shingle beach south of Ibiza Town. Beautiful people, super-yachts, and excellent beach restaurants.

restaurants.name: El Chiringuito
restaurants.pexels_q: luxury beach restaurant paella seafood Ibiza
restaurants.note: The most chic beach restaurant in Ibiza. Grilled fish and paella on the most beautiful naturist beach.

restaurants.name: Sa Capella
restaurants.note: In a converted 17th-century chapel. One of the most atmospheric and romantic dining settings.

restaurants.name: La Paloma
restaurants.note: A beautiful organic garden restaurant in the quiet north. Everything grown nearby. Legendary breakfast.

restaurants.name: Wild Beets
restaurants.note: The best vegetarian food in the Balearics — but non-vegetarians love it too.

restaurants.name: Atzaró Agroturismo
restaurants.pexels_q: orange grove estate garden dining Ibiza
restaurants.note: In a 300-year-old orange grove estate. Pool-side lunch and romantic garden dinner.

restaurants.name: Lio
restaurants.pexels_q: dinner show cabaret Mediterranean Ibiza entertainment
restaurants.note: Dinner theatre Ibiza-style — Mediterranean food, live performance, then DJs.

restaurants.name: Bar Costa
restaurants.pexels_q: traditional Spanish Ibiza bar food local
restaurants.note: The soul of old Ibiza — an art-filled bar in the most beautiful interior village.

restaurants.name: Es Rebost de Can Prats
restaurants.pexels_q: traditional Ibizan food stew local restaurant
restaurants.note: The most authentic traditional Ibizan restaurant in town. Sofrit pagès and greixonera.

restaurants.name: Mirador de Dalt Vila
restaurants.note: On the terrace of the old town with panoramic views over the port. Perfect for sunset.

restaurants.name: Los Enamorados
restaurants.pexels_q: boutique restaurant local seafood Ibiza north
restaurants.note: The best restaurant in the quiet north. Fresh, local, beautifully presented.

rentals.name: Avis / Europcar (Ibiza airport)
rentals.desc: Recommended for exploring the north and west — the best coves are inaccessible without a car.

rentals.name: Ibiza Moto (multiple locations)
rentals.desc: The most popular way to get around. Easy parking, good for cove-hopping. Book ahead in July–August.

rentals.name: Ibiza Boat Charter
rentals.desc: Half-day and full-day private boat charters to access the most secluded coves in the southwest.

rentals.name: DiscoBar (DJ Bus)
rentals.desc: Night buses connecting the main clubs from all major resorts. The safest way to move between clubs.

accommodation.why: The most beautiful base — UNESCO old town, excellent restaurants, harbour nightlife.
The chicest village — art galleries, organic restaurants, and boutique fincas.
The most family-friendly and relaxed resort — a pretty promenade, calm beaches.
The quiet, bohemian north. Fincas, organic food, and wild coves. Far from the clubs.

tips.title: Ibiza in July and August is extremely expensive
tips.text: Hotels, restaurants, and clubs charge three or four times the off-season rate. June and September offer the same weather for far less.

tips.title: The north is a completely different island
tips.text: The northern parishes are the authentic, quiet Ibiza — organic farms, deserted coves, and none of the club infrastructure.

tips.title: Club tickets should be booked online in advance
tips.text: The major clubs charge much less for online tickets. Prices range from €30 to €100+.

tips.title: Driving at night after clubs is dangerous
tips.text: Use the DiscoBar night bus network — it connects all the main venues safely.

tips.title: Go to the beaches in the morning
tips.text: The most beautiful beaches (Cala Conta, Cala Xarraca) are at their best before 11am.

formentera.name: Formentera
formentera.tagline: Caribbean water, barefoot luxury & ancient seagrass
formentera.description: Formentera is what the rest of the Mediterranean used to look like before mass tourism arrived. The smallest of the four main Balearic Islands, accessible only by ferry from Ibiza, it has the clearest, most luminous water in the western Mediterranean — beaches of such fine white sand and such brilliant turquoise colour that visitors regularly mistake photos for the Caribbean. There are no airports, almost no traffic lights, and a strict building height limit that has prevented the high-rise development that has ruined so much of the Spanish coast.
formentera.ferry: Ibiza → La Savina (Formentera) — 30 mins / multiple daily sailings
activities: Cycling the island in a day
Pilar de la Mola artisan market
formentera.funfact: The Posidonia oceanica seagrass meadows surrounding Formentera are estimated to be up to 100,000 years old — among the oldest living organisms on Earth.
hero_queries: Cala Saona red cliffs cove Formentera

sights.name: Ses Illetes
sights.desc: A narrow sandbar peninsula of powder-white sand and Caribbean-blue water — consistently named among the best beaches in Europe.

sights.name: La Mola Lighthouse
sights.desc: A 19th-century lighthouse at the eastern tip on sheer 100m cliffs. The most dramatic viewpoint in Formentera — magnificent at sunset.

sights.name: Posidonia Seagrass Snorkelling
sights.desc: The UNESCO-protected seagrass meadows around Formentera are among the most extensive in the Mediterranean. Snorkel over them to see sea horses, octopus, and dense fish life.

sights.name: Sant Francesc Xavier
sights.desc: The small, charming capital — a fortified 18th-century church, a hippie market, and the most genuine village café culture in the Balearics.

sights.name: Pilar de la Mola Market
sights.desc: A weekly artisan market in the La Mola plateau village — handmade jewellery, woven textiles, and local produce.

beaches.name: Ses Illetes
beaches.desc: The iconic Formentera beach — a narrow peninsula of white sand with turquoise water on both sides. Regularly listed in the top 10 beaches in Europe.

beaches.name: Platja de Llevant
beaches.desc: The eastern side of the Ses Illetes peninsula — wider, wilder, with a naturist section. Calmer water and fewer people.

beaches.name: Cala Saona
beaches.desc: A sheltered cove between red cliffs in the west. Calm, clear, and beautiful — the most romantic cove in Formentera.

beaches.name: Ses Platgetes d'es Pujols
beaches.desc: The most accessible beach near the main resort. Fine sand, calm water, good facilities.

beaches.name: Cala en Baster
beaches.desc: A tiny, rarely-visited cove in the northeast accessible on foot or by bicycle. Rocky, wild, very clear water.

restaurants.name: Juan y Andrea
restaurants.note: The most famous restaurant in Formentera — feet in the sand, wood-fired paella, clearest water in Spain.

restaurants.name: Es Moli de Sal
restaurants.pexels_q: creative Mediterranean seafood tasting menu Formentera
restaurants.note: The most refined restaurant on the island. Creative tasting menus using local fish.

restaurants.name: Can Dani
restaurants.pexels_q: traditional Formentera fish stew Balearic food
restaurants.note: The definitive traditional restaurant in the capital. Bullit de peix (fish stew) and grilled fish.

restaurants.name: Blue Bar
restaurants.pexels_q: bohemian beach bar live music Formentera
restaurants.note: A legendary bohemian beach bar with a long tradition of live music and good vibes.

restaurants.name: Sa Platgeta
restaurants.note: On the beach at Es Pujols. Fresh fish from local boats, good paella.

restaurants.name: Restaurante Mirador de la Mola
restaurants.pexels_q: lighthouse cliff restaurant sea view Formentera
restaurants.note: At the La Mola lighthouse. Simple, fresh food with extraordinary cliff views. Unforgettable sunset.

restaurants.name: Can Rafalet
restaurants.note: On a working fishing harbour on the north coast. Whatever came in that morning is on the menu.

restaurants.name: Chezz Gerdi
restaurants.note: The coolest restaurant in Es Pujols — eclectic Mediterranean dishes in a beautiful garden.

restaurants.name: La Gondola
restaurants.note: Italian-owned with genuinely good pasta and pizza alongside Formentera seafood.

restaurants.name: Tanga Bar
restaurants.pexels_q: luxury beach bar cocktails white sand
restaurants.note: The most stylish beach bar on Ses Illetes. Cold drinks, good music, beautiful people.

rentals.name: Moto Rent Formentera (La Savina)
rentals.desc: Formentera is made for cycling — flat, small, and with dedicated bike paths linking the whole island.

rentals.name: Multiple agencies (La Savina port)
rentals.desc: All rentals based at the La Savina ferry port. Scooters perfect — no hills, no traffic.

rentals.name: Formentera Boat Hire
rentals.desc: Small motorboat hire to access secluded coves. No licence required for boats under 6m.

rentals.name: Trasmapi / Baleària
rentals.desc: Multiple daily ferries from La Savina to Ibiza (30 min). Book return tickets ahead in August.

accommodation.why: Closest to the famous beach and the best restaurants. Compact and walkable.
A small cluster of hotels above the most romantic cove. Very peaceful and beautiful.
The elevated eastern plateau — cooler, quieter, best sunsets. Rural fincas.
The island capital — most central base for cycling in any direction.

tips.title: Book your ferry return ticket in advance
tips.text: August ferries back to Ibiza can be completely full. Book a return ticket before you arrive.

tips.title: Cycle everywhere — it is the right speed for this island
tips.text: Formentera is small, flat, and has excellent cycle paths. A day's cycling covers the whole island.

tips.title: Sun is intense — the white sand reflects UV
tips.text: The pale sand and clear water amplify UV radiation. Factor 50+ is not excessive.

tips.title: The snorkelling is some of the best in Europe
tips.text: The Posidonia seagrass and crystal-clear water make Formentera outstanding for snorkelling.

tips.title: There are almost no large hotels
tips.text: Formentera has strict planning restrictions. Most accommodation is small agriturismos. Book months ahead for July–August.

menorca.name: Menorca
menorca.tagline: UNESCO biosphere, wild north & Caribbean south
menorca.description: Menorca is the quietest and most unspoilt of the four main Balearic Islands — a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve where tourism is deliberately controlled and the natural landscape protected. The island has an extraordinary contrast between coasts: the north is wild and rocky, battered by the Tramontana wind, with dramatic cliffs and rugged coves; the south is sheltered and almost tropical, with shallow turquoise lagoons and powder-white sand beaches. Two charming historic capitals — Mahón and Ciutadella — and a dense spread of Talayotic prehistoric monuments complete a picture of an island that does everything right.
menorca.ferry: Barcelona → Mahón (~9 hrs) / Valencia → Mahón (~8 hrs)
menorca.funfact: Menorca was under British rule for most of the 18th century, which is why Mahón harbour has a gin tradition — the British navy introduced it, and Menorcan gin (Xoriguer) is still distilled here today.
hero_queries: Camí de Cavalls coastal path Menorca

sights.name: Ciudadella Old Town
sights.desc: The former capital of Menorca — a beautiful historic centre of golden limestone palaces, Gothic cathedral, and labyrinthine streets. The most beautiful town in the Balearics after Palma.

sights.name: Naveta des Tudons
sights.desc: A perfectly preserved prehistoric burial chamber (1000 BC) shaped like an upturned boat. One of the most important and best-preserved megalithic monuments in the western Mediterranean.

sights.name: Camí de Cavalls
sights.desc: A 185km coastal path that circles the entire island — an ancient cattle trail now a world-class hiking and cycling route. No other Balearic island has this.

sights.name: Mahón Harbour & Gin Distillery
sights.desc: The second-largest natural harbour in the world after Pearl Harbor. The Xoriguer gin distillery has been producing Menorcan gin since the 18th century — tours and tasting available.

sights.name: Talati de Dalt
sights.desc: One of the finest Talayotic archaeological sites on the island — a taula (T-shaped stone monument), stone circles, and ancient burial chambers in a beautiful rural setting.

beaches.name: Cala Macarella
