beaches.desc: The most beautiful beach in Menorca — a sheltered cove of white sand, turquoise water, and limestone cliffs covered in pine. Access on foot or by boat.

beaches.name: Cala Turqueta
beaches.desc: Named for its turquoise water — a wide, sheltered cove of brilliant turquoise reached through a pine forest. One of the best natural beaches in Spain.

beaches.name: Son Bou
beaches.desc: The longest beach on the island — 2.5km of fine sand with ancient ruins (4th-century basilica) at one end. Good facilities and calm water.

beaches.name: Cala en Porter
beaches.desc: A dramatic beach in a narrow gorge — the sand is reached by descending steep steps. Spectacular setting, very sheltered.

beaches.name: Cavalleria Beach (north)
beaches.desc: Wild, exposed, and windy — a dramatic experience of the unspoilt north coast. Rusty cliffs, rough waves, and extraordinary scenery.

restaurants.name: Café Balear
restaurants.note: A Menorcan institution — the best place on the island for caldereta de llagosta (spiny lobster stew).

restaurants.name: Ca N'Olga
restaurants.note: In a renovated farmhouse in the countryside. Slow-cooked Menorcan dishes and excellent local cheese.

restaurants.name: Ses Forquilles
restaurants.note: The most creative kitchen in the capital. Modern interpretations of Menorcan classics with excellent wine.

restaurants.name: Es Cranc
restaurants.note: In the fishing village of Fornells — famous for its lobster caldereta. King Juan Carlos would arrive by yacht for lunch here.

restaurants.name: La Minerva
restaurants.note: Floating restaurant in Mahón harbour on a converted boat. Beautiful setting and good fresh fish.

restaurants.name: Molí de Foc
restaurants.note: In a restored windmill just outside Mahón. Traditional Menorcan cooking and good local wines.

restaurants.name: Es Tast de na Sílvia
restaurants.pexels_q: creative Mediterranean small plates tapas Menorca
restaurants.note: Creative small plates and excellent local wine selection in Ciutadella. A favourite with food lovers.

restaurants.name: Bar Triton
restaurants.pexels_q: Spanish seafood bar mezze harbour village
restaurants.note: Simple, genuine seafood bar in the fishing village of Fornells. Fresh crab, prawns, and cold beers.

restaurants.name: Ca Na Pilar
restaurants.note: Generous portions of traditional Menorcan food at honest prices in the capital.

restaurants.name: Bar Ulisses
restaurants.pexels_q: Spanish beach bar grill food summer
restaurants.note: Reliable beach bar near Cala Turqueta with good grilled food and cold drinks.

rentals.name: Avis / Hertz (Menorca airport)
rentals.desc: Essential for reaching the secluded beaches and prehistoric sites. The south coast beaches require a car.

rentals.name: Velo Menorca (Mahón & Ciutadella)
rentals.desc: The Camí de Cavalls is a world-class cycling route around the whole island. Bikes, e-bikes, and route guides available.

rentals.name: Menorca Nautica
rentals.desc: Half-day and full-day boat charters to access the most secluded southern coves from the sea.

rentals.name: Camí de Cavalls Guided Walks
rentals.desc: Guided sections of the famous coastal path — cliffs, coves, and prehistoric monuments. Excellent for day walks.

accommodation.why: The most beautiful and atmospheric town. The most characterful restaurants and golden limestone architecture.
The capital and most practical base — ferry port, best shopping, harbour restaurants, airport access.
Beautiful southern resort area close to the best beaches. Calm, family-friendly.
Charming fishing village on the north coast — famous for lobster stew and a beautiful harbour. Perfect for a peaceful, local experience.

tips.title: Menorca is the Balearics' best-kept secret
tips.text: Far fewer tourists than Mallorca or Ibiza, strict environmental protection, and genuinely beautiful. One of the most underrated islands in the Mediterranean.

tips.title: The Camí de Cavalls is extraordinary
tips.text: The 185km coastal path circles the entire island. Walk a section for a completely different perspective on Menorca.

tips.title: The Tramontana wind can be brutal
tips.text: The cold north wind makes the north coast uninhabitable in winter and rough in summer. The south coast is always calmer.

tips.title: Order the lobster caldereta in Fornells
tips.text: Menorcan spiny lobster stew (caldereta de llagosta) is one of the great dishes of Spain. It's expensive but worth it. Order it in Fornells.

tips.title: Try Xoriguer gin with lemon
tips.text: Menorcan gin has been made in Mahón since the 18th century. A gin-lemon (pomada) is the island's signature drink.

malta.name: Malta
malta.tagline: Ancient temples, baroque cities & crystal coves
malta.description: Malta is the smallest country in the European Union and one of the most historically dense places on Earth. A rocky limestone archipelago in the centre of the Mediterranean, it has been fought over by Phoenicians, Romans, Arabs, Normans, Knights of St John, Napoleon, and the British — each leaving an extraordinary layer of history. The capital Valletta is the smallest EU capital city and a UNESCO World Heritage Site of astonishing Baroque architecture. The prehistoric temples of Malta are older than Stonehenge and the Egyptian pyramids, and the Blue Lagoon on Comino island is one of the most beautiful and instantly recognisable spots in the Mediterranean.
malta.ferry: Sicily (Pozzallo) → Malta (~1.5 hrs) / Catania → Malta (3.5 hrs)
malta.funfact: Malta's prehistoric temples at Ħaġar Qim and Mnajdra (3600–3200 BC) are among the oldest free-standing stone structures on Earth — older than Stonehenge by 1,000 years.

sights.name: Valletta
sights.desc: The smallest capital city in the EU — a UNESCO World Heritage Baroque city built by the Knights of Malta in the 16th century. Walk the main street, visit St John's Co-Cathedral (with Caravaggio originals), and take the Grand Harbour ferry.

sights.name: Ħaġar Qim & Mnajdra Temples
sights.desc: Prehistoric temples dating to 3600 BC — older than the Egyptian pyramids. On a clifftop overlooking the sea. Among the most important prehistoric sites in the world.

sights.name: Blue Lagoon (Comino)
sights.desc: A stunning turquoise lagoon on the tiny island of Comino, accessible by ferry from Malta or Gozo. One of the most photographed spots in the Mediterranean.

sights.name: Mdina — the Silent City
sights.desc: A perfectly preserved medieval walled city on a hilltop. Almost no cars, beautiful palaces and churches, and extraordinary views over the whole island.

sights.name: The Three Cities (Vittoriosa, Senglea, Cospicua)
sights.desc: Three ancient fortified cities across the harbour from Valletta. More atmospheric and less touristy than the capital, with extraordinary maritime history.

beaches.name: Blue Lagoon (Comino)
beaches.desc: The iconic turquoise lagoon on Comino island. Shallow, crystal-clear, extraordinary colour. Day trips from Malta and Gozo run every morning.

beaches.name: Golden Bay
beaches.desc: The most popular sandy beach in Malta — a long crescent of golden sand with calm water and good facilities. Beautiful especially in the late afternoon.

beaches.name: Mellieħa Bay
beaches.desc: The largest sandy beach in Malta — long, gentle, and ideal for families. Clear water and good facilities.

beaches.name: St Peter's Pool
beaches.desc: A natural swimming hole carved into the limestone rock on the southern coast. No sand, but crystal-clear deep water and dramatic rock formations.

beaches.name: Ramla Bay (Gozo)
beaches.desc: The best beach in Gozo — reddish sand, clear water, and the impressive ruins of a Roman villa at one end. A ferry from Malta followed by a short drive.

restaurants.name: Noni
restaurants.pexels_q: modern Maltese fine dining creative food
restaurants.note: The best restaurant in Valletta. Creative Maltese cuisine using local ingredients in an elegant setting.

restaurants.name: Guze Bistro
restaurants.note: Serving genuine Maltese home cooking in the capital. Bragioli (beef olives), fenkata (rabbit), and local wine.

restaurants.name: Tal-Familja
restaurants.pexels_q: Maltese rabbit traditional food village restaurant
restaurants.note: One of the most beloved traditional restaurants in Malta. The rabbit (fenek) is extraordinary. Book ahead.

restaurants.name: Beppe's
restaurants.note: Long-established seafood institution in the capital. Excellent fresh fish from local boats.

restaurants.name: Rubino
restaurants.note: Classic Maltese cooking in Valletta since 1906. The most historically significant restaurant on the island.

restaurants.name: Il-Kartell
restaurants.pexels_q: Maltese harbour fish market fresh seafood
restaurants.note: In the famous Sunday fish market village. Excellent fresh catch from local fishermen at honest prices.

restaurants.name: Tmun Mgarr
restaurants.note: The best restaurant in Gozo. Fresh local seafood and traditional Gozitan dishes.

restaurants.name: De Mondion
restaurants.pexels_q: Mediterranean fine dining rooftop terrace view
restaurants.note: Rooftop restaurant on the bastion walls of Mdina. Extraordinary views and refined Mediterranean cooking.

restaurants.name: Fumia
restaurants.note: Contemporary cooking using Maltese ingredients in creative ways. Good wine list.

restaurants.name: The Harbour Club
restaurants.note: On the waterfront opposite Valletta. Excellent views of the Grand Harbour and good food.

rentals.name: Multiple agencies (Malta airport)
rentals.desc: Very useful for reaching the temples, beaches, and the south of the island. Traffic in Valletta and Sliema is dense.

rentals.name: Gozo Channel Line
rentals.desc: Regular ferries from Ċirkewwa to Gozo (25 min). Gozo is a different, quieter island — a must-visit.

rentals.name: Multiple operators (Valletta & Gozo)
rentals.desc: Day trips to the Blue Lagoon on Comino. Departures from Sliema, Valletta, and Gozo every morning.

rentals.name: Malta Public Transport
rentals.desc: Malta has an extensive bus network connecting all towns. Affordable and surprisingly good.

accommodation.why: Staying in the UNESCO capital is extraordinary — Baroque palaces converted into boutique hotels. Walk to everything.
The main resort and nightlife area. Waterfront promenade, best range of restaurants and bars, good transport links.
The quietest and most scenic part of Malta. Good beaches, a pretty town, and less traffic.
The smaller, quieter sister island. Dramatically different atmosphere — more rural, more traditional. Day trip or overnight stay.

tips.title: Malta is a year-round destination
tips.text: With mild winters and little rain, Malta is one of the few Mediterranean destinations genuinely pleasant outside summer. The shoulder seasons are ideal.

tips.title: English is an official language
tips.text: Malta is fully bilingual (Maltese and English). There is no language barrier whatsoever for British or international English-speaking visitors.

tips.title: Driving is on the left
tips.text: Malta follows British driving convention — cars drive on the left. Roads in Valletta and Sliema are very congested.

tips.title: Visit Gozo — it's very different to Malta
tips.text: Gozo is quieter, greener, and has a more traditional rural character. The Ramla Bay beach and the Ggantija temples are outstanding. Easy day trip by ferry.

tips.title: Valletta is a Baroque jewel
tips.text: St John's Co-Cathedral contains two Caravaggio originals. The city was built by the Knights of Malta in the 16th century and has barely changed.

ischia.name: Ischia
ischia.tagline: Thermal spas, volcanic beaches & Neapolitan luxury
ischia.description: Ischia is the volcanic island in the Bay of Naples that Capri overshadows — a mistake, because Ischia is larger, wilder, more varied, and in many ways more satisfying. It is Italy's premier spa island, with natural hot springs and thermal parks that have attracted visitors since Roman times (Emperor Augustus was a regular). The island combines volcanic beaches of dark sand, a dramatic medieval castle on its own small island, mountain hiking to the summit of an extinct volcano, and some of the best seafood restaurants in southern Italy. Visitors who discover Ischia often find it preferable to the more famous, more crowded, and more expensive Capri.
ischia.ferry: Naples → Ischia Porto (1.5 hrs) / Pozzuoli → Ischia (1 hr fast ferry)
ischia.funfact: Ischia's thermal waters have been used medicinally since at least the Roman era — the Greek physician Hippocrates himself recommended them. The waters emerge at temperatures up to 165°C.

sights.name: Aragonese Castle (Castello Aragonese)
sights.desc: One of the most extraordinary sights in southern Italy — a medieval castle built on a volcanic rock connected to the main island by a stone bridge. The views over the Bay of Naples are incredible.

sights.name: Poseidon Thermal Gardens
sights.desc: The largest and most beautiful thermal park on the island — 22 pools of thermal water at different temperatures, a spa, and a beach, all within a beautifully landscaped subtropical garden.

sights.name: La Mortella Gardens
sights.desc: Created by Lady Walton (wife of composer William Walton) — arguably the most beautiful private garden in Italy. Subtropical plants, a Roman bath, and extraordinary views.

sights.name: Mount Epomeo
sights.desc: The extinct volcanic summit of the island (788m) — reachable on foot or by donkey. The views over the Bay of Naples to Vesuvius and Capri are extraordinary.

sights.name: Sant'Angelo village
sights.desc: A tiny, car-free fishing village on the southern coast — whitewashed houses, boats in the harbour, excellent restaurants, and natural thermal springs bubbling up on the beach.

beaches.name: Citara Beach
beaches.desc: Below the Poseidon Thermal Gardens — a wide sandy beach with natural hot thermal water bubbling through the sand. A warm-water swimming experience unlike any other.

beaches.name: Maronti Beach
beaches.desc: The longest beach on the island — 2km of dark volcanic sand on the south coast. Beautiful, with natural steam vents on the beach. Accessible by boat or steep path.

beaches.name: San Montano Bay
beaches.desc: A sheltered, beautiful bay on the north coast. Shallow, calm, turquoise water. The Negombo thermal park is right here.

beaches.name: Cartaromana Beach
beaches.desc: Below the Aragonese Castle — a small, sheltered bay with natural thermal springs on the seabed. Extraordinary natural jacuzzi experience.

beaches.name: Lacco Ameno
beaches.desc: A beautiful curved bay with a distinctive mushroom-shaped volcanic rock (Il Fungo) emerging from the sea. Calm, clear, and elegant.

restaurants.name: Il Focolare
restaurants.pexels_q: traditional Italian island food rabbit wine
restaurants.note: The most beloved traditional restaurant on the island. The coniglio all'Ischitana (Ischian rabbit) is legendary. Book weeks ahead.

restaurants.name: Ristorante Cava dell'Isola
restaurants.pexels_q: Italian seafood fine dining cliffside restaurant
restaurants.note: Perched on the rocks at Sant'Angelo. Exceptional fresh seafood with extraordinary views.

restaurants.name: Da Coco
restaurants.pexels_q: Italian seafood pasta clams fresh harbour
restaurants.note: The most reliable seafood restaurant in the port area. Spaghetti alle vongole is perfect.

restaurants.name: Umberto a Mare
restaurants.pexels_q: Italian cliffside sea view restaurant seafood
restaurants.note: A Forio institution on the rocks above the sea. Spectacular views, excellent seafood, romantic setting.

restaurants.name: Alberto Restaurant
restaurants.pexels_q: Italian restaurant harbour seafood fresh fish
restaurants.note: An Ischia classic since 1949. Fresh fish and excellent pasta in the port area.

restaurants.name: La Calajanara
restaurants.pexels_q: traditional Italian home cooking pasta meat
restaurants.note: Generous traditional Italian cooking near the thermal area. Excellent value and genuinely delicious.

restaurants.name: Bistrot Ischia
restaurants.note: A modern bistro in the port. Good wine, interesting small plates, and a relaxed atmosphere.

restaurants.name: Il Giardino delle Ninfe
restaurants.pexels_q: Italian garden restaurant outdoor dining evening
restaurants.note: Dinner in a beautiful garden setting in Forio. Romantic, well-executed Italian cooking.

restaurants.name: Da Nando
restaurants.pexels_q: traditional Italian island food pasta meat
restaurants.note: Classic Ischian cooking at honest prices. The polpo (octopus) alla Luciana is outstanding.

restaurants.name: La Taverna del Re
restaurants.note: Good all-round seafood restaurant in the port. Reliable cooking with a solid wine list.

rentals.name: Multiple agencies (Ischia Porto)
rentals.desc: The most popular way to explore the island. The roads are manageable and a scooter gives complete freedom.

rentals.name: Ischia Car Rentals
rentals.desc: A small car is useful for accessing the mountain roads and the less accessible south coast.

rentals.name: Ischia Boat Tours
rentals.desc: Half-day and full-day tours around the island visiting sea caves, hot spring beaches, and the thermal bays.

rentals.name: Poseidon / Negombo / Aphrodite
rentals.desc: Day passes to the thermal park complexes. Pools at different temperatures, spas, and beach access.

accommodation.why: The most beautiful and atmospheric village on the island — car-free, charming, thermal springs on the beach.
The most popular resort area with good beaches, excellent restaurants, and the La Mortella gardens nearby.
The main town and ferry port. Best transport connections, good restaurants, the castle is right here.
The most elegant and upscale resort area — exclusive hotels, thermal parks, and a beautiful bay.

tips.title: The thermal parks are the main event
tips.text: Poseidon and Negombo are both extraordinary — full days spent between hot pools, the sea, and a spa. Book ahead in high season.

tips.title: Getting to Ischia is easy from Naples
tips.text: Multiple ferries daily from Naples Molo Beverello and Pozzuoli. The hydrofoil takes 35 minutes, the car ferry 1.5 hours.

tips.title: Try coniglio all'ischitana — the local dish
tips.text: Ischian-style rabbit braised with white wine, tomatoes, herbs, and olives is the defining dish of the island. Every good restaurant makes it.

tips.title: Driving in summer is stressful
tips.text: The roads are narrow and summer traffic is heavy. Consider leaving the car behind and using the bus, taxis, and boats.

tips.title: Visit the castle in the late afternoon
tips.text: The Aragonese Castle is most beautiful in the late afternoon light. Combine with a sunset aperitivo at the castle café.

cyprus.name: Cyprus
cyprus.tagline: Aphrodite's island — ancient ruins, beaches & halloumi
cyprus.description: Cyprus is where the goddess Aphrodite was born from the sea — at least according to mythology — and the island has a divine quality to match: long sandy beaches, ancient ruins of extraordinary importance, dramatic mountain forests, and a cuisine built around halloumi, mezze, and excellent local wine from grapes grown since antiquity. The island is divided since 1974 and the north is under Turkish control, but the south — the internationally recognised Republic of Cyprus — has world-class archaeological sites, a beautiful old town in Lefkara, and the legendary Troodos Mountains.
cyprus.ferry: Limited commercial ferry connections — most visitors fly
cyprus.funfact: Cyprus gives its name to copper — the Latin 'cuprum' derives from 'Kypros', because the Romans sourced most of their copper here. The island has been mined for copper since 4000 BC.
hero_queries: Petra tou Romiou Aphrodite rock Cyprus
Fig Tree Bay beach Protaras Cyprus
gallery_queries: Petra tou Romiou Aphrodite rock Cyprus

sights.name: Paphos Archaeological Park (UNESCO)
sights.desc: An extraordinary concentration of Roman-era mosaics right by the sea — considered the finest in the eastern Mediterranean. The Tomb of the Kings is also nearby.

sights.name: Petra tou Romiou (Aphrodite's Rock)
sights.desc: A dramatic sea stack on the western coast where Aphrodite is said to have risen from the sea. One of the most iconic and photographed spots in Cyprus.

sights.name: Kourion Ancient Theatre
sights.desc: A magnificently preserved Greek theatre on a clifftop above the sea. Still used for performances in summer. The nearby beach is one of the best on the island.

sights.name: Troodos Mountains & Wine Villages
sights.desc: The forested mountain interior — entirely unexpected on a sun-drenched Mediterranean island. Byzantine painted churches (UNESCO), cool air, and wine villages producing excellent Commandaria.

sights.name: Lefkara Village
sights.desc: A beautiful medieval lace-making village in the hills. The intricate silverwork and lace (lefkaritika) made here has been inscribed on UNESCO's cultural heritage list.

beaches.name: Nissi Beach
beaches.desc: The most famous beach in Cyprus — a sandy cove with a small island reached by a sandbar. Busy and lively, especially in the morning.

beaches.name: Fig Tree Bay (Protaras)
beaches.desc: A beautiful curved sandy bay — consistently one of the top-rated beaches in Europe. Clear water, good facilities, beautiful setting.

beaches.name: Governor's Beach
beaches.desc: A dramatic beach of white chalk cliffs meeting dark sand and blue water. Unusual and striking geology near Limassol.

beaches.name: Coral Bay
beaches.desc: A wide, well-organised sandy bay near Paphos. Calm, clear water, good facilities. Excellent for snorkelling.

beaches.name: Kourion Beach
beaches.desc: Below the ancient theatre — a long stretch of exposed coast with some shade. One of the finest beach-and-ancient-ruins combinations in the Mediterranean.

restaurants.name: Voreas
restaurants.note: The most creative kitchen in the north of Cyprus (Republic side near Polis). Outstanding modern takes on Cypriot classics.

restaurants.name: 1900 Art Café
restaurants.note: The most beloved café-restaurant in the old Nicosia. A true meze experience in a beautiful courtyard.

restaurants.name: Militzis
restaurants.note: One of the most celebrated traditional meze restaurants in Cyprus. More than 30 dishes arrive at your table.

restaurants.name: Old Town Tavern
restaurants.note: Reliable, generous Cypriot cooking in the heart of old Paphos. Lamb souvlaki, halloumi, and local wine.

restaurants.name: Imogen's Inn
restaurants.pexels_q: Cypriot mountain village food wine traditional
restaurants.note: In the beautiful wine village of Omodos. Excellent kleftiko (slow-cooked lamb), local wine.

restaurants.name: Ristorante Mediterraneo
restaurants.note: The best fine dining restaurant in Limassol. Excellent seafood and a good Cypriot wine list.

restaurants.name: Pyrofani Restaurant
restaurants.pexels_q: Cypriot seafood fresh fish larnaca harbour
restaurants.note: Best fish taverna in Larnaca. Fresh catch, good mezze, and views over the salt lake.

restaurants.name: Seven St Georges Tavern
restaurants.pexels_q: traditional Cypriot food lamb meze garden
restaurants.note: Garden setting in old Paphos. Traditional Cypriot dishes at honest prices.

restaurants.name: Ammos
restaurants.pexels_q: Mediterranean beach restaurant seafood Ayia Napa
restaurants.note: On the beach in Ayia Napa. Good seafood and salads with your feet practically in the sand.

restaurants.name: Arsinoe Fish Tavern
restaurants.pexels_q: Cypriot fish taverna harbour fresh seafood
restaurants.note: Simple, excellent seafood in the harbour of Polis. Fresh fish at unbeatable prices.

rentals.name: Multiple agencies (Larnaca & Paphos airports)
rentals.desc: A car is essential in Cyprus. Driving is on the left (British convention). The mountains and west coast require a car.

rentals.name: Cyprus Moto Rentals (Paphos, Ayia Napa)
rentals.desc: Good for exploring the coast around individual resorts. Not suitable for the mountain roads.

rentals.name: Sea Cruises Cyprus (Paphos & Ayia Napa)
rentals.desc: Day trips to Aphrodite's Rock, Coral Bay, and the sea caves. Multiple operators from all main resorts.

rentals.name: OSEA / Intercity buses
rentals.desc: Good intercity bus network connecting Nicosia, Larnaca, Paphos, and Limassol. Cheap and reliable.

accommodation.why: The most interesting base — ancient ruins, a lovely harbour, and good beaches. Better atmosphere than the east-coast resorts.
The most cosmopolitan city in Cyprus. Excellent food scene, upscale marina, and the most sophisticated nightlife.
The best beaches in Cyprus. Lively resort area — best beaches in Cyprus but very touristy.
The most unspoilt area of the Republic of Cyprus. Wild, beautiful, and less developed. Near the Akamas Peninsula.

tips.title: Cyprus drives on the left
tips.text: British convention — cars drive on the left. A legacy of British rule (1878–1960). Easily adjusted to within a day.

tips.title: Understand the island's division
tips.text: The northern part of Cyprus is under Turkish administration since 1974 and not internationally recognised. You can cross at checkpoints. The south (Republic of Cyprus) is EU and the tourist infrastructure is entirely there.

tips.title: Commandaria is one of the world's oldest wines
tips.text: Cyprus produces Commandaria — a sweet dessert wine made since antiquity. Richard the Lionheart called it "the wine of kings" in 1191. Try it in the Troodos wine villages.

tips.title: Halloumi cheese is a Cypriot invention
tips.text: Halloumi originated in Cyprus and the island is the only place authorised to export it as PDO-protected halloumi. The fresh, unpackaged version is extraordinary.

tips.title: Cyprus is very hot in summer
tips.text: July and August can reach 40°C in Nicosia. The coast is bearable; the mountains are pleasantly cool. Early May, October, and November are ideal.

naxos.name: Naxos
naxos.description: Naxos is the Cyclades island that hasn't sold out. The largest Cycladic island is also the most fertile, producing its own cheese, potatoes, olive oil, and marble. Long sandy beaches with barely anyone on them, mountain villages where locals invite you to share their table, and an ancient marble gateway at sunset that has stood for 2,500 years — Naxos represents what the Cyclades were like before the crowds arrived, and it still has that character.
naxos.ferry: Athens (Piraeus) — 5.5 hrs ferry / 3.5 hrs fast ferry
naxos.funfact: Naxos is the only Cycladic island nearly self-sufficient in food — it produces its own cheese, potatoes, olive oil, and marble, and has done so since antiquity.

sights.name: Portara (Temple of Apollo)
sights.desc: The massive marble doorway of an unfinished 6th-century BC temple on a tiny islet connected to town by a causeway. One of the most iconic sunset spots in Greece.

sights.name: Naxos Town (Hora)
sights.desc: The island's capital — a maze of Venetian-era alleys, a hilltop castle, excellent restaurants, and boutique shops.

sights.name: Chalki Village & Kitron Distillery
sights.desc: The most beautiful inland village — Byzantine churches, Venetian towers, and the Vallindras distillery producing kitron, a liqueur unique to Naxos.

sights.name: Kouros of Apollonas
sights.desc: A colossal unfinished 10-metre marble statue abandoned in a quarry 2,600 years ago. Lies where it fell, in the open air, free to visit.

sights.name: Venetian Castle (Kastro)
sights.desc: The medieval Venetian fortress crowning Naxos Town, with Catholic churches, mansions, and a small archaeological museum.

beaches.name: Agios Prokopios
beaches.desc: Fine white sand, calm clear water, good facilities. Consistently voted one of the best beaches in the Cyclades.

beaches.name: Plaka
beaches.desc: 5km of pristine white sand dunes — remote undeveloped sections feel like a private beach. Mornings are perfect.

beaches.name: Mikri Vigla
beaches.desc: Famous twin beaches — one calm, one windy — with a dramatic rocky headland between them. World-class kite-surfing.

beaches.name: Agia Anna
beaches.desc: Walking distance from Agios Prokopios — lively beach village with tavernas and watersports.

beaches.name: Aliko
beaches.desc: Wild and undeveloped cedar forest meets the sea. Naturist-friendly, remote, magical atmosphere.

restaurants.name: Scirocco
restaurants.note: Rooftop terrace with exceptional creative dishes using Naxian ingredients. Best in town.

restaurants.name: Taverna Plateia
restaurants.pexels_q: Greek village square taverna outdoor food
restaurants.note: In the village square under a plane tree. Outstanding home cooking — lamb and local graviera.

restaurants.name: Axiotissa
restaurants.pexels_q: Greek mountain village food goat wine
restaurants.note: In the highest village on Naxos. Goat dishes, local wine, unforgettable mountain views.

restaurants.name: To Elliniko
restaurants.note: Beloved local spot. Proper Greek food at honest prices. No frills, no tourist menu.

restaurants.name: Metaxi Mas
restaurants.pexels_q: Greek mezze seafood Cycladic islands food
restaurants.note: Terrace overlooking the sea. Excellent mezze and Naxian specialities.

restaurants.name: Grill House Gialos
restaurants.pexels_q: Greek grill souvlaki beach taverna meat
restaurants.note: By the beach. Superb grilled meats and a cheerful atmosphere.

restaurants.name: Ouzeri Naxos
restaurants.pexels_q: Greek ouzo bar mezze seafood afternoon
restaurants.note: Laid-back ouzo bar with an excellent mezze selection. Perfect for a lazy afternoon.

restaurants.name: Juicy
restaurants.pexels_q: Greek breakfast fresh juice yogurt honey
restaurants.note: Best breakfast and juice bar on the island. Fresh fruits and local honey.

restaurants.name: Kavouri
restaurants.note: Harbourfront seafood. Fresh fish, grilled octopus, and classic Greek mezze.

restaurants.name: The Old Inn
restaurants.note: German-owned and surprisingly excellent. Mixed menu in a lovely garden setting.

rentals.name: Multiple agencies at Naxos port
rentals.desc: A car is ideal for mountain villages and remote beaches.

rentals.name: Naxos Bikes & ATVs
rentals.desc: Scooters for coastal routes, ATVs for interior tracks.

rentals.name: Naxos Kite Pro (Mikri Vigla)
rentals.desc: Kite and windsurfing lessons and equipment rental at Mikri Vigla.

rentals.name: Naxos Walking Tours
rentals.desc: Guided walks through the Kastro, mountain villages, and ancient marble quarries.

accommodation.why: Best base — castle, restaurants, nightlife, ferry access, and the Portara all within walking distance.
Right next to the best beach. Quieter and more relaxed than Hora.
Stunning inland village for a truly different stay. Converted mansions, total peace.
Beach village feel with tavernas, bars, and watersports.

tips.title: Afternoon meltemi winds can be strong
tips.text: The northerly meltemi picks up in July–August and can make north-facing beaches uncomfortable.

tips.title: Taste everything local
tips.text: Naxian graviera cheese, local potatoes, kitron liqueur, and fresh thyme honey are all island specialities.

tips.title: Buses serve the main beaches
tips.text: KTEL buses run frequently from Hora to Agios Prokopios and Agia Anna (€1.80). Car needed for mountains.

tips.title: Best value in the Cyclades
tips.text: Naxos is significantly cheaper than Santorini or Mykonos while being arguably more beautiful and authentic.

tips.title: Plaka can have rough surf
tips.text: The southern part of Plaka is exposed to ocean swell. Swim in the calmer northern sections if conditions are rough.

paros.name: Paros
paros.description: Paros hits the sweet spot between lively and authentic, stylish and genuine. It offers the best nightlife in the Cyclades outside Mykonos, excellent beaches for every type of swimmer, a charming capital in Parikia, and Naoussa — one of the prettiest fishing harbour villages in all of Greece. The island also serves as the best base for island hopping — ferries connect easily to Naxos, Milos, Santorini, and the smaller islands.
paros.ferry: Athens (Piraeus) — 4.5 hrs ferry / 3 hrs fast ferry
paros.funfact: Parian marble was used to sculpt both the Venus de Milo and the Nike of Samothrace — two of the most famous sculptures in the world, both now in the Louvre in Paris.

sights.name: Naoussa Village
sights.desc: A fishing harbour of whitewashed houses, Venetian castle ruins, boutique restaurants, and excellent nightlife. One of the most beautiful harbour villages in the Cyclades.

sights.name: Ekatontapiliani (Church of 100 Doors)
sights.desc: A remarkable 4th-century Byzantine church in Parikia — one of the best-preserved early Christian monuments in Greece.

sights.name: Lefkes Village
sights.desc: The most beautiful inland village — marble-paved alleys, twin-towered church, and a 5km Byzantine footpath to Prodromos.

sights.name: Butterfly Valley (Petaloudes)
sights.desc: A lush green valley where thousands of tiger moths gather in summer — a peaceful and beautiful natural detour.

sights.name: Antiparos Island
sights.desc: A tiny island a 10-minute ferry from Parikia. Quiet beaches, a famous stalactite cave, and a charming village.

beaches.name: Golden Beach (Chryssi Akti)
beaches.desc: World-class windsurfing beach. 700m of golden sand, clear water, watersports, tavernas.

beaches.name: Kolymbithres
beaches.desc: Unique beach near Naoussa with smooth granite rock formations. Calm, shallow, beautiful.

beaches.name: Faragas
beaches.desc: Tiny, sheltered, turquoise — one of the most beautiful small beaches on the island.

beaches.name: Santa Maria
beaches.desc: Wild north coast beach with a hip beach bar, consistent wind, and a beautiful sunset point.

beaches.name: Logaras
beaches.desc: Quiet beach near Piso Livadi. Gentle waves, a local taverna, and far fewer people than the main beaches.

restaurants.name: Barbarossa
restaurants.pexels_q: Greek harbour seafood Cyclades grilled fish
restaurants.note: Right on the harbour in Naoussa. One of the best seafood restaurants in the Cyclades.

restaurants.name: Soso
restaurants.pexels_q: modern Greek tasting menu fine dining Cyclades
restaurants.note: Creative tasting-menu restaurant. Exceptional quality — book weeks ahead.

restaurants.name: Levantis
restaurants.pexels_q: fusion Mediterranean Asian Greek food creative
restaurants.note: Hidden gem in Parikia's old town. Inventive menu blending Greek and Asian influences.

restaurants.name: Tamarisko
restaurants.pexels_q: Greek mezze taverna generous portions grilled
restaurants.note: Beloved local taverna. Generous mezze, great grilled fish, honest prices.

restaurants.name: Glafkos
restaurants.pexels_q: Greek mountain village food goat stew wine
restaurants.note: In the beautiful mountain village. Goat stew, local wine, cool air. Worth the drive.

restaurants.name: Porphyra
restaurants.pexels_q: Greek fish restaurant waterfront Cyclades seafood
restaurants.note: Excellent fish restaurant on the Parikia waterfront.

restaurants.name: Yabanaki
restaurants.pexels_q: Greek street food wrap casual late night
restaurants.note: Casual, vibrant, excellent. Great for a late-night bite after the Naoussa harbour.

restaurants.name: Ephesus
restaurants.note: Romantic garden restaurant near the harbour. Known for lamb and creative starters.

restaurants.name: Symposium
restaurants.pexels_q: Greek wine cellar Cycladic mezze tasting
restaurants.note: Excellent wine list focusing on Cycladic wines.

restaurants.name: Clumsies at Paros
restaurants.pexels_q: craft cocktail bar small plates Mediterranean Greece
restaurants.note: Athens' most famous cocktail bar has a Paros outpost. Excellent drinks and small plates.

rentals.name: Multiple agencies (Parikia & Naoussa)
rentals.desc: Makes exploring Lefkes and remote beaches much easier.

rentals.name: Paros Kite & Wind Club (Golden Beach)
rentals.desc: The windsurf capital of the Aegean. Lessons, equipment rental, and coaching for all levels.

rentals.name: Local ferry (Parikia)
rentals.desc: Short passenger ferry from Parikia to Antiparos every 30 minutes.

rentals.name: Sea Kayak Paros
rentals.desc: Guided kayak tours along the rocky coastline visiting sea caves and hidden coves.

accommodation.why: The most charming village. Best restaurants, prettiest harbour, and best nightlife.
The capital — best for ferry access, most practical. Great old town, all budgets.
South coast village — calmer pace, great beach, local fish tavernas.
North coast — quieter, by a beautiful beach, far from the crowds.

tips.title: Naoussa gets very busy in August
tips.text: The harbour fills in peak season. June and September are far more pleasant.

tips.title: Paros is a major Cyclades ferry hub
tips.text: Blue Star Ferries stop here — excellent base for island hopping.

tips.title: Golden Beach has world-class wind conditions
tips.text: The reliable afternoon meltemi makes it one of the best windsurfing spots in Europe.

tips.title: Naoussa has excellent nightlife
tips.text: Genuinely good bars and clubs — great for couples who want evening energy without the Mykonos madness.

tips.title: The island is perfect for a scooter
tips.text: Paros is the right size for scootering. The main coast road is well-maintained and all highlights are reachable in a day.
